# Hectare 5 — Firmware 1.0.20

# What the Hectare 5 system does

The seeding control system with the Hectare 5 panel watches sowing and the application of dry and liquid fertilizer on seed drills and planters. Where the machine has dispenser electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump, it also drives them, so that the set rate is actually applied.

![The Hectare 5 panel. It is operated by touch only.](figures/five-panel)

The panel sits in the cab and is operated with the fingers on its screen — it has no buttons. Everything else is on the implement: one seed sensor per section, and whatever the machine needs besides. What your machine carries is entered in the [profile](profile.md); the screens show exactly that.

## Seed

- Applies seed to the rate the operator sets, through the dispenser electric motors.
- Watches the actual sowing against that rate and reports a section that falls behind.
- Reports a blocked or empty tube **by its number**.
- Counts seeds, **doubles and skips** in the **“Precise”** mode — on row-crop planters.

## Dry and liquid fertilizer

- Applies liquid fertilizer to the rate through the electric pump.
- Watches dry and liquid lines and reports a section that falls behind or blocks, by number.

## The machine around the product

- Hopper level, dispenser shaft rotation, fan speed, air pressure or vacuum, travel speed — each against its own limits.
- The sensors of an autonomous fan-drive engine: oil pressure, battery charge, ignition, fuel level, air filter.
- Working or transport position of the implement, and the markers.

## Tramline

- Creates the tramline with actuators or by stopping dispenser motors.
- Advances the bout by itself from the marker sensors or the work position sensor.
- Keeps watching the sections that are shut off, so that a section sowing into the tramline is still reported.

## Speed from the built-in GPS receiver

The panel has a GPS receiver of its own. It can take the travel speed from the satellites instead of a wheel sensor, and it shows how many satellites it sees. See [GPS](gps.md).

## Records

- Treated area, split into sown, not sown and unknown.
- Detailed statistics of the work, kept for five fields.
- Reports written to the memory card.

> **NOTE**
>
> The system applies **one product in the “Precise” mode** (seeds per metre), **up to four products by mass** (kilograms per hectare) and **one liquid product** (litres per hectare).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The panel](front-panel.md) · [Quick start](quick-start.md) · [Terms](terms.md)


# The panel and its touch screen

The Hectare 5 has **no buttons**. Everything is done with the fingers on the screen: taps, touch-and-hold, swipes, and taps with two or three fingers. What each gesture does on each screen is in [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).

![The Hectare 5 panel with the home screen. The screen texts in this picture are not in English.](figures/five-panel)

## The screen

- **800 × 480 colour screen** with a touch surface. It recognises up to three fingers at once — which is how the panel tells a tap from a two-finger or a three-finger tap.
- **Brightness** is set by hand, in steps of 10 %, in the Settings menu. There is no automatic brightness. See [Set the screen brightness](screen-brightness.md).
- **Sound.** The panel clicks on every touch it recognises, if **“Buttons sound”** is set to **“Yes”** in the Settings menu. A gesture that the screen in front of you does not use gives no click. Alarms have their own sound, and the panel beeps when seeding starts and stops.

## Built into the panel

| **Part** | **What you see of it** |
| --- | --- |
| **microSD card slot** | A card symbol on the home screen while a card is ready. Reports are written to the card. See [Memory card](indicators.md#memory-card). |
| **Clock with its own battery** | The time of day at the top right of the home screen. A weak clock battery shows as **BAT**. See [Clock](indicators.md#clock). |
| **GPS receiver** | A satellite symbol in the right-hand column of the home screen, with the number of satellites. It can serve as the speed source. See [GPS](gps.md). |

> **TIP**
>
> **A touch the panel does not expect is ignored, not misread.** Each screen listens only to its own gestures. If nothing happens, check the gesture — a swipe too short, a finger lifted too early — before you suspect the panel.

How the screens, menus and windows work: [Menus, context menus, number pad and windows](interface-basics.md).


# Switching on

When the panel gets power, a start screen with the logo appears. The start screen stays until every device connected to the panel has answered — usually a few seconds, at most about fifteen — and then the [home screen](home-screen.md) opens.

![The start screen.](figures/five-boot)

> **NOTE**
>
> **If the start screen stays about fifteen seconds,** the panel has been waiting for a device that does not answer. Nothing is broken yet — but look at the home screen and the alarms as soon as it appears. See [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## What state the panel starts in

- **Access level: Operator.** The panel starts at the Operator level after every power-on, whatever level was set before. Switching off and on is therefore also the quickest way back to Operator — the only level at which alarm windows are shown. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).
- **The ordinary home screen.** The [second home screen](second-home-screen.md) is never opened by itself; you open it by hand.
- **Application locked, if the speed is imitated.** If speed imitation is switched on in the speed sensor and the machine has dispenser electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump, the panel starts with product application **locked by hand**. Unlock it when you are ready: [Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

The firmware version and the serial number can be read at any time: two-finger tap on the home screen, then **“About”** in the main menu. The window closes with **“Close”**.

## Before switching off

- **Settings** are stored by themselves a few seconds after your last change. Wait a few seconds after changing a setting before you switch the panel off.
- **The statistics** are written every five minutes and when the machine stops. **Switch the panel off only after you have stopped moving** — otherwise the last stretch of work is lost from the [statistics](statistics-screen.md).


# Menus, context menus, number pad and windows

Everything on the panel happens through five things: the **working screens**, the **main menu**, the **context menu** of a device, the **number pad** and the **windows** that ask or tell you something. All of them are worked with the fingers; the gestures are listed in [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md). The working screens have their own topic: [Working screens](working-screens.md).

## The main menu

Tap the home screen with **two fingers**. The main menu opens over the home screen, with its first item selected. On the second home screen, a tap on the settings symbol does the same.

::: {.anatomy fig="five-main-menu"}
1. **Selected item.** Black text on a blue band. Here **“Fill the disks with seeds”** — see [Fill the disks](fill-the-disks.md).
2. **“Settings”.** The settings of the system and of the machine. See [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).
3. **Arrow head.** The item opens another menu.
4. **“Service”.** Commissioning and service items. Shown from the Agronomist level up.
5. **“About”.** A window with the firmware version and the serial number of the panel; **“Close”** closes it.

The main menu of a planter with dispenser motors in the “Precise” mode, standing still, at the Agronomist level.
:::

**Working a menu by touch:**

- **Tap** an item to select it — the blue band moves to it.
- **Tap the selected item again** to enter it: it opens its menu, runs its action or opens the number pad. **Touch and hold** an item does both at once.
- **Swipe right or left** anywhere over the menu to raise or lower the value of the **selected** item. A short stroke changes it by one step; a longer one goes on stepping as the finger travels. The swipe always changes the item on the blue band, not the one under your finger. Lists of words go round: after the last word comes the first.
- **Swipe up or down** to scroll a long menu.
- **Tap outside the menu**, on the darkened screen, to leave it. A tap with three fingers does the same.

An item is read by what stands on its right. The marks **-** and **+** appear around the value of the selected item only.

| **What you see on the right** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| An arrow head **>** | The item opens another menu. Tap it again. |
| A value between **-** and **+** | Swipe right to raise it, left to lower it, right there in the list. |
| A value between **-[** and **]+** | A swipe, or a second tap, opens the number pad. |
| **!** | The item writes over stored values: it zeroes the statistics, saves or loads settings, sets a device, or resets values to their defaults. Tap it again. |
| Nothing | The item performs an action. Tap it again. |

![The Seeding machine parameters menu: the width in square brackets opens the number pad; the modes change in the list; the two calibrations are actions.](figures/five-param-edit)

Settings are stored by themselves a few seconds after the last change; there is nothing to save.

## The context menu of a device

Every sensor, motor and indicator on the home screen has its own menu. **Touch and hold the device** — its icon or its column on the diagram — for more than half a second, and its context menu opens. A short tap does nothing. On the Motors screen and on the second home screen the same works for a motor tile.

![The context menu of a seed sensor.](figures/five-ctx-seed)

The first item, **“Information”**, opens the status screen of the device; there a swipe right or left shows the next or the previous device, and a swipe up or a three-finger tap returns. The second item switches the control: **“Disable control”** or **“Enable control”** — see [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). Below them stand the parameters; which ones you see depends on the access level ([Access levels](access-levels.md)). All parameters: [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

## Entering numbers

When a value is written between square brackets, changing it opens the number pad.

::: {.anatomy fig="five-number-pad"}
1. **Name of the parameter.** Here **“Width, cm”**.
2. **Value.** What you have typed so far.
3. **Backspace.** Deletes the last digit. Touch and hold it to clear the whole value.
4. **Digits.** **1** to **9**.
5. **Point key.** Adds the decimal point — only for a value that has decimals.
6. **Zero.**
7. **“OK”.** Accepts the value.

The number pad. A tap outside the pad leaves without changing anything.
:::

A value outside the permitted range is not refused: the panel sets the nearest limit instead.

## Windows that ask, and windows that tell

A window is a box in the middle of the screen with a **coloured strip** along its top — without a word in it — and the message under the strip.

| **Window** | **What it is** | **How it closes** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Blue strip, buttons below** | The panel asks. Nothing happens until you answer. | Touch **“Yes”** (green) or **“No”** (red). A touch outside the box cancels: nothing is changed. |
| **Blue strip, no buttons** | The panel tells you what happened. | Some close by themselves after about two seconds, others with a touch inside the box. |
| **Red strip, no buttons** | The panel reports an error, for example **“Invalid PIN”**. | As above. |
| **Red strip and a red bar with “FAILURE!”** | An alarm. | See below. |

A question window ignores touches during the first half second, so that the touch that opened it does not answer it.

![A question window: the blue strip, the question, Yes and No.](figures/five-question)

## Alarm windows

An alarm window says **what happened**, **on what kind of device**, and **which devices** — their numbers are listed when several identical sensors report the same fault, for example **#1-4,7**. While it is open, the panel sounds the alarm.

![An alarm window with the Close button.](figures/five-alarm-window)

**Touch “Close” in the window.** This alarm closes and the sound stops; the next alarm in the queue appears. Nothing else closes an alarm window — touches elsewhere are ignored.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Closing the window stops the sound, not the fault.** Alarms are closed one at a time, and they are shown **only at the Operator level**. What each alarm means: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).


# Quick start — getting ready and moving off

Your machine may not have every step — skip what it does not have. The main menu opens with a **two-finger tap** on the home screen; a device's context menu with a **touch and hold** on the device ([Interface basics](interface-basics.md)).

## Before the field

::: steps
1. **Calibrate the speed sensor.** Area, rates and deviations are all calculated from the speed; a wrong speed makes every other figure wrong. Standing still, touch and hold the speed field and choose **“Speed calibration”** — at the Operator level. The same item is under **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**, at the Agronomist level. See [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).

2. **Calibrate the metering rollers** — on machines that apply products by weight. From the context menu of each dispenser (**“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**, shown when its weight control is on) or of each dispenser motor, at the Operator level, standing still. See [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

3. **Check the tramline rhythm**, if the machine makes tramlines. See [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

4. **Check the sensor parameters** — the list is below.

5. **Check each section**: is it under control, does it apply product. See [The four states of a section](section-states.md#the-four-states-of-a-section).

6. **Choose the field** on the Statistics screen: two-finger tap, **“Select field”**. For a new field, erase its statistics first with **“Zero statistics”**. See [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md#the-menu-of-the-screen).

7. **Set the rates** — seeding, dry fertilizer, liquid fertilizer. See [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

8. **Check the access level.** It must be **“Operator”**: **“Settings”** → **“User”**.
:::

Several of these settings need the Agronomist level — **“Seeding machine parameters”** among them. Raise the level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)), do what needs it, drop back to Operator, do the rest.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Step 8 is the one that ruins a day.** From the Agronomist level upwards the panel shows **no alarm windows but one**: a blocked tube is not reported. The one that still comes through is **“User is Agronomist! Alarms will not be shown!”** — raised **once**, when seeding starts at that level. Faults that are still present are reported once you are back at Operator. Check the level before every start, not once a season.

### Sensor parameters to check

- **Speed sensor** — “Min speed, km/h”, “Max speed, km/h”.
- **Dispenser sensor** — “Period, s”, for each sensor.
- **Fan sensor** — “Minimum, rpm”, “Maximum, rpm”, for each sensor.
- **Pressure sensor** — “Minimum, Pa”, “Maximum, Pa”, for each sensor.
- **Liquid fertilizer pump** — “Pulses per liter”, “Max pressure, Bar”.
- **Seed and dry fertilizer sensors** — “Fraction”, “Correction”, “Recalculation,m” or “Recalculation,sec”; in the “Precise” or “Hybrid” mode also “Rate error,%”.
- **Electric motors, “Precise” mode** — “Holes in disk”.
- **Electric motors, dosing by weight** — for each motor, “Weight, gr” and “Rotations”. The mass calibration fills both in.

Details: [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

## Moving off

::: steps
1. Put the implement into the **working** position.

2. **Planters with dispenser motors:** fill the disks — main menu, **“Fill the disks with seeds”**. Without it the first metres of every row are empty. See [Fill the disks](fill-the-disks.md).

3. **Grain drills:** nothing to start. The metering motors begin turning by themselves as soon as the product application control starts — the moment you move off.

4. Drive.
:::

> **WARNING**
>
> **Filling the disks and starting the motors turn machinery while the machine stands still.** Make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts or the fan.

**When the control starts.** The manual lock must be **off** ([Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)). If a work position sensor is fitted and under control, the control begins once you move with the implement lowered; without such a sensor, as soon as you move. Alarms start after the delay set in **“Settings”** → **“Alarm delay”**, 2 to 20 seconds.

| **Sound** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| One short beep | The panel sees the machine seeding. From now on the sections are watched. |
| Three short beeps | The seeding has stopped — at the headland, or the columns have sunk under the control line. |

On grain drills in the “Flow” or “Hybrid” mode, let the panel find the alarm level itself: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).

## While working

Watch four things: the **speed** against the tractor, the **fan and the pressure** inside their range, the **actual rate** against the target, and that no sensor is alarming. The [Table screen](table-screen.md) shows how each section is doing right now; the [Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md) how the whole field has gone.

If the speed sensor fails, see [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).


# About the pictures in this manual

The screens in this manual are being shot on a Hectare 5 panel on a test bench. Until a frame is taken, its place carries the words **Picture to follow**. The text around it describes the screen in words — top row, right-hand column, rate field — so that every topic can be used without its picture.

The photograph of the panel is a product picture. The texts on its screen are not in English; the layout of the home screen is the same.

## The words on your screen

This manual quotes every label exactly as the English panel shows it — including spellings that look unusual, such as **“Factical”** and **“Setuped”** on the Statistics screen, or **ks/Ha** for thousands of seeds per hectare. Look for the words as printed here.

## What belongs to the bench

A bench panel shows a few things your panel will not. When the frames arrive, read them with this table.

| **What you see in a picture** | **Why it is there** | **What your panel shows instead** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A blue time in the clock slot, then **TRIAL**, then blank | The bench panel runs on a trial licence; the blue figure is the time left. | The time of day. See [Clock](indicators.md#clock). |
| **IMITAT** in yellow in the clock slot | The bench runs in an imitation mode of the service menu. | The time of day. |
| A yellow speed figure, or **IMITATION** in the speed field | The speed is simulated, not measured — there is no wheel turning on a bench. | The measured speed in white. See [Speed](indicators.md#speed). |
| Columns that move although the machine stands still | The seed flow is imitated on the bench. | Columns that move only while seeding. |
| Red hoppers, a red oil can or battery | The bench has no product and no engine. | Green icons while everything is in order. |
| A red actuator symbol in the right-hand column | Actuators named in the bench profile are not fitted, so the panel reports them as faulty. | Nothing — the symbol is not shown while every actuator is in order. See [Actuator failure](indicators.md#actuator-failure). |
| A red **×** in place of an icon | A device named in the bench profile is not connected. | The icon of the device. |
| Zeros on the Statistics screen | The bench statistics were empty when the frame was taken. | Your figures. |


# The home screen

The home screen is the main working screen. It shows the diagrams of the section control sensors, the state indicators of the devices and the key figures of the work. What it shows follows the [profile](profile.md): every group of sensors and devices entered there gets its icons, its columns, its rate field.

The screen has four zones. The **travel speed** stands large at the top left. The **indicator rows** run along the top, with the **clock** at the top right. A **column of indicators** runs down the right-hand edge. The lower part holds the **diagrams** — one column per section — each with its **rate field** on the right.

## A grain drill with seed and fertilizer

::: {.anatomy fig="five-home-flow"}
1. **Travel speed.** In km/h. Messages about the speed replace the figure. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
2. **Hoppers.** One icon per hopper sensor, numbered. Red — the level is below the sensor. [Hopper](indicators.md#hopper)
3. **Metering units.** Rotation of the dispenser shafts; the icon turns while the shaft turns. [Metering unit](indicators.md#metering-unit)
4. **Fan.** The fan icon and its speed in rpm. [Fan](indicators.md#fan)
5. **Engine sensors.** Oil pressure, battery charge and ignition of the fan-drive engine. [Engine sensors](indicators.md#engine-sensors)
6. **Clock.** The time of day; the slot also carries messages. [Clock](indicators.md#clock)
7. **Memory card.** Shown while a microSD card is ready. [Memory card](indicators.md#memory-card)
8. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field. [Area](indicators.md#area)
9. **Product rate by weight.** The rate of a product, in kg/ha. [Product rate by weight](indicators.md#product-rate-by-weight)
10. **Seed diagram.** One column per seed sensor; the white line is the control line. [The section diagram](section-diagram.md)
11. **Rate field.** Measured rate on top, target below, here in seeds per second. [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md)
12. **Fertilizer diagram.** The fertilizer sections, with their own rate field.
13. **Right-hand column.** Implement position, manual lock, satellites, actuator failure — whichever the machine has. [Indicators](indicators.md)
14. **Section numbers.** The number of each section, under its column.

A drill with seed and fertilizer rows, standing still: targets set, actual rates zero.
:::

## A planter at work

::: {.anatomy fig="five-home-precise"}
1. **Travel speed.** [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
2. **Hopper.** Green — product above the sensor.
3. **Pressure.** Vacuum or positive pressure in kPa. [Pressure](indicators.md#pressure)
4. **Area.** Hectares treated on the active field.
5. **Population.** The actual seeding rate in thousands of seeds per hectare. [Population](indicators.md#population)
6. **Section column.** Green — the row sows within its tolerance. [Column colours](section-states.md#column-colours)
7. **Skips bar.** Yellow hatching on the left of a column: the share of skips in that row.
8. **Doubles bar.** Blue hatching on the right of a column: the share of doubles.
9. **Rate line.** The target rate across all rows.
10. **Tolerance ticks.** Upper and lower limit of the permitted deviation, in every column.
11. **Rate field.** Measured seeds per metre on top, target below.
12. **Implement position.** Green — lowered, in work. [Implement position](indicators.md#implement-position)

An eight-row planter in the “Precise” mode, seeding.
:::

What each indicator means in all its states is in [Indicators](indicators.md); the diagram itself — line, ticks, colours — in [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).

## What you can do from the home screen

| **To do this** | **Do this** |
| --- | --- |
| Open the main menu | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Change the target rate or the alarm level | Touch and hold the diagram, then swipe up or down — [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md) |
| Set the target of a product by weight | Touch and hold its kg/ha indicator; the number pad opens |
| Let the panel set the alarm level | **Double tap**, while applying — [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md) |
| Lock or unlock product application | Touch and hold an empty place of the right-hand column — [Lock application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md) |
| Open the settings of a device | Touch and hold its icon or column |
| Go to the next working screen | **Long swipe left** — [Working screens](working-screens.md) |
| Open the second home screen | **Long swipe right** — [Second home screen](second-home-screen.md) |

A long swipe runs across more than a third of the screen. All gestures on all screens: [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).


# The section diagram — columns, line and colours

Each column of the diagram is one section — one seed or fertilizer sensor. Its height is the flow through that section. How the rest is drawn depends on the seeding control mode: **“Precise”** (seeds per metre, with skips and doubles) or **“Flow”** (seeds per second against an alarm level). The rate field stands at the right end of each diagram: the measured figure on top, the target or alarm level below it, the unit under them.

## “Precise” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="five-diagram-precise"}
1. **Target rate.** Grey, in seeds per metre (**s/m**). This is the figure you change by touch.
2. **Measured rate.** White — the average of the rows now.
3. **Scale of the bars.** The share of skips or doubles at which a bar reaches the top — **“Scale S&D,%”** in the settings.
4. **Rate line.** The target, drawn across all rows.
5. **Upper tick.** The upper limit of the tolerance, in each column.
6. **Lower tick.** The lower limit of the tolerance.
7. **Column.** Green — the row sows within the tolerance.
8. **Skips bar.** Yellow hatching on the left edge of a column. The taller it is, the more skips in that row.
9. **Doubles bar.** Blue hatching on the right edge of a column. The taller it is, the more doubles.
10. **Section number.**

An eight-row planter seeding; some rows skip, some double.
:::

## “Flow” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="five-home-flow-at-work"}
1. **Alarm level.** Grey, in seeds per second (**s/s**). The level under which a section counts as losing flow.
2. **Measured rate.** White — the average of the rows now.
3. **Control line.** The alarm level, drawn across all rows.
4. **Column above the line.** Green — the row works.
5. **Empty part of a column.** Dark grey above the green: the higher the green reaches, the more flow.
6. **Section numbers.** Fertilizer sections continue after the seed sections.
7. **Fertilizer diagram.** The same, for the fertilizer sensors.
8. **Fertilizer rate field.** Measured on top, alarm level below, in fertilizer per second (**f/s**).

A drill with seed and fertilizer rows, seeding. Every column stands above its line.
:::

To change the target or the alarm level, **touch and hold the diagram** until its target figure lights up, then swipe up or down — one step per swipe. A tap outside the diagrams ends it. See [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

## The line: rows under it are not under control

The line is the boundary of a partial blockage, not a decoration. A column above the line is a row that works; a column that sinks under it is a row that is losing flow — long before it blocks completely.

::: {.anatomy fig="five-home-not-under-control"}
1. **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”.** The rows of this diagram are not watched.
2. **Columns under the line.** Every row delivers less than the level.
3. **Control line.** Dragged above the real flow.
4. **Alarm level.** Higher than the machine sows.
5. **Measured rate.** Lower than the alarm level.

A drill with the alarm level set too high. The diagrams have dropped out of control.
:::

**“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** opens no alarm window; at the Operator level the panel sounds the alarm instead. Rows under the line are not under control on purpose: the panel refuses to guard a level that was set above what the machine really delivers. Lower the level until the columns stand above the line, or let the panel set it with a double tap: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).

Whether the machine is seeding at all, the panel decides by the **share of rows that are seeding** — the sensor setting **“Percent of sowing,%”**, 20 % by default. On the headland the rows drop out of control; on the next pass they come back, with or without a work position sensor. The panel says so with sound: **three short beeps** when the seeding stops, **one short beep** when it starts again.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Read the columns against the line, not against each other.** Above the line the section works. Down at the line it does not — whatever the neighbours do.

What every colour and symbol of a column means, and the four states of a section: [Column colours and section states](section-states.md).


# Column colours and the four states of a section

How the diagram is built — rate line, ticks, control line — is in [The section diagram](section-diagram.md). This page lists what a single column can look like.

## Column colours

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Green column | The row sows normally. |
| Blue column | The row sows **more** than the target allows (“Precise” and “Hybrid”). |
| Yellow column | The row sows **less** than the target allows (“Precise” and “Hybrid”). |
| Background blinking dark red, no column | The row sows almost nothing while the machine is seeding — a blocked or empty tube. |
| White column with **!** | The control of this section is switched off. Nothing about it is watched. |
| Red **×** | The sensor does not answer. |
| Red **?**, column blinking red | A device of the wrong kind answers in place of this sensor. |
| Yellow **?** | The sensor has just received its settings, or it counts seeds but the panel has no speed to judge them by. |
| Grey hatching over the whole column | The section is shut off for the tramline, or its product application is switched off. |
| Green hatching at the bottom of a grey column | A small flow in a shut-off section, still within what is tolerated. |
| Red hatching in a grey column | The shut-off section sows into the tramline. |

![A diagram with a section out of control, a silent sensor and a shut-off section.](figures/five-diagram-states)

## The four states of a section

Each section has two independent switches: whether the panel **watches** it (control), and whether the machine **applies** through it (product application).

| **Control** | **Application** | **What it means** | **What the column shows** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| on | on | Normal work. | The normal column. |
| on | off | The row deliberately does not sow — a tramline row — and the panel knows it. | Grey hatching. |
| off | on | The row sows, but nobody is checking it. | White with **!** |
| off | off | The section is out of the work altogether. | White with **!** |

Both switches are items of the sensor's context menu — touch and hold the column of the section:

- **“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”**, at the Operator level. See [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).
- **“Product application”**, at the Agronomist level. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A white column with ! looks quiet, but it is blind.** Whatever happens in that row — a blocked tube, a broken sensor — the panel reports nothing.


# Indicators of the home screen

Where each indicator sits is shown in [The home screen](home-screen.md). This page says what each one means, state by state. Touch and hold any indicator to open the context menu of its device.

## How to read any indicator

![](figures/icons/fan.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/fan-red.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/no-connection.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/not-controlled.png){height=40px}

Almost every indicator follows the same rule. Learn it once and you can read an indicator you have never seen.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/fan.png){height=32px} **Green** icon | Normal. The device answers and its value is inside the limits. |
| ![](figures/icons/fan-red.png){height=32px} **Red** icon, blinking | Alarm. The device answers, but the value has left the limits. An alarm window follows after the alarm delay. |
| ![](figures/icons/no-connection.png){height=32px} Icon alternating with a **red ×** | No answer from the device. The value is shown as **XXXX**. |
| ![](figures/icons/not-controlled.png){height=32px} Icon alternating with a **white [!]** | The device is in the profile, but its control is switched off. The value is shown as **!!!!**. |
| Icon alternating with a red **?** | A device of the wrong kind answers in its place. The value is shown as **????**. |
| ![](figures/icons/work-blocked.png){height=32px} **Yellow** icon | Not a fault. A state you have chosen or that needs your attention: implement raised, markers up, ignition off, application locked by hand. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A switched-off indicator is not a quiet one — it is a blind one.** White with **!!!!** means the panel does not watch that device at all. Nothing will be reported about it, however wrong it goes.

## Speed

The travel speed in km/h, large, at the top left. Messages about the speed replace the figure and blink about once a second, so that the figure stays readable.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| A number in white, e.g. **10.0** | Normal. |
| **“SLOWER”** on red | You drive faster than the maximum set for the speed sensor. Slow down. |
| **“FASTER”** on red | You drive slower than the minimum. Speed up. |
| **XX.X** in red, blinking | No answer from the device that carries the speed sensor. |
| **????** in red | A device of the wrong kind answers in place of the speed sensor. |
| **!!.!** in white | The speed sensor is not under control. |
| A yellow number alternating with **“IMITATION”** | The speed is simulated from the setting of the speed sensor, not measured. See [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md). |
| **INCREASE IMITATION** / **DECREASE IMITATION** | The simulated speed itself is outside the permitted range. Change the setting, not the travel speed. |
| **“Sensor”** with a number | One of two speed sensors has failed. |
| **“Settings”** | The minimum and the maximum speed contradict each other. |

**“SLOWER”** and **“FASTER”** are not alarm windows. They stay in the speed field for as long as the speed is wrong, because you have to see them while correcting it. Speed from the built-in receiver: [GPS](gps.md).

## Clock

The clock slot at the top right is shared by several messages.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| The time in white | Normal. |
| **BAT** in red, for about a second in every four | The clock battery is low. The clock still runs; between the flashes the time is shown in red. Have the battery replaced. |
| **XX:XX** in red, blinking | The clock chip does not answer. Everything the panel records carries a wrong date and time. |
| **IMITAT** in yellow | The imitation mode of the service menu is on. |
| Blue hours:minutes, then **TRIAL**, then blank | A trial period is running; the blue figure is the time left. |

The clock is set in **“Settings”** → **“Change Date&Time”**: tap each line and swipe it to its value, then tap **“Set”** twice — once to select it, once to store the time. Leaving without **“Set”** keeps the old time.

## Memory card

![](figures/icons/microsd.png){height=40px}

A card symbol next to the clock, or in the right-hand column. Shown while a microSD card is in the slot and ready to be written to.

## Hopper

![](figures/icons/bunker-full.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/bunker-empty.png){height=40px}

A **full green** hopper is normal. An **empty red** one, blinking, means the level has fallen below the sensor: refill.

## Metering unit

![](figures/icons/dosator.png){height=40px}

The rotation of the dispenser shaft. While the shaft turns, the icon **turns** — the fastest way to see that the metering unit really runs. Red means no rotation, or not the speed required.

## Fan

![](figures/icons/fan.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/fan-red.png){height=40px}

The fan speed in revolutions per minute (**rpm**). Green is normal; red — above the maximum or below the minimum.

## Pressure

![](figures/icons/pressure.png){height=40px}

The vacuum or the positive air pressure in the distribution system, in **kPa**. Green is normal; red — outside the permitted range.

## Engine sensors

![](figures/icons/ignition.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/oil.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/battery.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/fuel.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/airfilter.png){height=40px}

The sensors of the engine that drives the fan.

| **Indicator** | **Green** | **Red or yellow** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oil pressure | Normal | **Red:** the oil pressure has fallen below the permitted level. |
| Battery charge | Normal | **Red:** the battery is not being charged. |
| Ignition | **Green key:** ignition on | **Yellow key:** ignition off. Not a fault, and never an alarm window. |
| Fuel level | Normal | **Red:** little fuel left in the tank. |
| Air filter | Normal | **Red:** the air filter is clogged; clean or replace it. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Oil pressure and battery charge are watched only while the ignition is on.** Fuel level and air filter are watched always.

## Area

![](figures/icons/area.png){height=40px}

The area treated on the [active field](statistics-screen.md), in hectares.

## Population

![](figures/icons/seeds.png){height=40px}

In the “Precise” mode: the actual seeding rate in **thousands of seeds per hectare**.

## Product rate by weight

![](figures/icons/product.png){height=40px}

Shown when products are applied by weight; one indicator per product, with its number. It shows **one figure**, in kg/ha.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Icon **green**, figure white | Normal. While the actual rate stays inside the permitted deviation, the figure shown is the target. |
| Icon **red**, blinking | The actual rate is outside the permitted deviation from the target. |
| Field lit | You have just set the target. |

To set the target, touch and hold the indicator. The number pad opens with the caption **Product** and its number; type the rate, 10.0 to 500.0 kg/ha, and touch **“OK”**.

## Dosing by weight is not possible

![](figures/icons/product.png){height=40px}

A **red blinking product icon** in the right-hand column. The panel has worked out that the target cannot be held at any travel speed: the lowest speed at which the metering rollers can deliver the rate is already at or above the highest.

**What to do.** Check the target rates first — one product asking too much closes the window for all of them. Then check the metering rollers. The speed limits the panel calculated are on the **“Information”** screen of the speed sensor.

## Markers

![](figures/icons/markers.png){height=40px}

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| **Green**, both arms down | Both markers are lowered. |
| **Green**, one arm down | Only that marker is lowered. |
| **Yellow**, both arms up | Both markers are raised. On a machine that changes the tramline bout by the markers, the bout changes now. |

A machine with one marker has one icon that shows that marker down or up.

## Implement position

![](figures/icons/work-allowed.png){height=40px} ![](figures/icons/work-blocked.png){height=40px}

**Green** — lowered, in work. **Yellow**, blinking — raised, in transport, not applying.

## Tramline bout

![](figures/icons/tramline.png){height=40px}

Shown only if the tramline is switched on. The large number is the current bout, the small one above it the number of bouts in the rhythm.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Tramline icon **grey** | The bout changes by itself at the end of every pass. |
| Tramline icon **yellow** | The bout does not change by itself: the machine has no marker or work position sensor that answers and is under control. |
| A yellow symbol blinking in place of the icon | The bout could change by itself, but automatic change is switched off. |

How the bout is counted: [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md#how-the-bout-changes).

## Manual lock

![](figures/icons/hand.png){height=40px}

A **yellow hand**, blinking, in the right-hand column: product application is locked by hand. The machine applies nothing, however it moves. Not shown while application is allowed. It appears on machines with dispenser electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump. See [Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

## Actuator failure

![](figures/icons/actuator-fail.png){height=40px}

One icon for all electric motors and tramline actuators together, in the right-hand column. **Not shown at all while everything is in order.**

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| **Red**, blinking | At least one motor or actuator is in an alarm state. |
| Alternating with **white [!]** | The control of at least one actuator is switched off. |

Which one and why is on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md).

## Liquid fertilizer pump

| **Indicator** | **What it shows** |
| --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-rate.png){height=32px} **Rate** | In **L/min** when the machine has liquid section sensors, otherwise in **L/Ha**. Green, red, × and [!] as usual. While the rate stays inside the permitted deviation, the figure shown is the target. |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-load.png){height=32px} **Load**, % | How hard the pump works. **Yellow at 99 % and above**: the pump is at its limit — drive slower, or the rate falls below the target. **----** blinking red: the controller gives no load figure. |
| ![](figures/icons/pump-pressure.png){height=32px} **Pressure**, **Bar** | Only if the pressure sensor is switched on in the pump settings. **Red: the liquid pressure is too high.** **----** blinking red: the pressure sensor is broken or gives no reading. |


# The built-in GPS receiver

The Hectare 5 has a GPS receiver of its own. The panel uses it in two ways: it shows how many satellites it receives, and — if it is set to — it takes the **travel speed** from the satellites instead of from a wheel sensor.

## The satellite symbol

On a machine with a speed sensor in the profile, a **satellite symbol** stands in the right-hand column of the home screen, with the number of satellites in use beside it.

| **What you see** | **What it means** |
| --- | --- |
| Satellite **grey** | The receiver works, but the speed is not taken from it. The number shows what it receives. |
| Satellite **green** | The speed comes from GPS; more than 6 satellites — a good signal. |
| Satellite **yellow** | The speed comes from GPS; 4 to 6 satellites. Usable, watch it. |
| Satellite **red** | The speed comes from GPS; fewer than 4 satellites. The speed cannot be trusted. |

![The satellite symbol in its four states — grey, green, yellow, red — with the number of satellites in use.](figures/five-gps-icon)

## Speed from GPS

Whether the speed comes from the receiver is the setting **“GPS internal”** in the context menu of the speed sensor (touch and hold the speed field). It needs the Agronomist level. See [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).

When GPS is the speed source and fewer than four satellites are received, the panel raises the alarm **“Poor GPS signal quality”**. Everything the panel calculates from the speed — area, rates, deviations, the drive of the dispenser motors — then depends on a weak signal. Move into the open, or switch back to the wheel sensor.

![The alarm of a weak GPS signal.](figures/five-gps-alarm-poor-signal)

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Under trees, buildings or a shed roof the receiver loses satellites.** Start the work only when the satellite symbol is green or yellow.

## The GPS screen

On the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md), a tap on the GPS symbol opens a screen with the receiver's own data: the speed it measures, the date and time it receives (UTC, not the local time of the panel), and the number of satellites in use and in view. Below them runs a log of the receiver for the service engineer. The texts on this screen are in English in every panel language. Leave it with a long swipe up.

![The GPS screen opened from the second home screen.](figures/five-gps-test)


# The second home screen

The second home screen shows the work in large figures and the dispenser motors as a row of tiles. It suits a machine whose seeding rate is held by dispenser electric motors, where the panel watches the motors and the main working units rather than a diagram of sections.

**Open it** from the home screen with a **long swipe to the right**. **Close it** with a **long swipe to the left** — it returns to the home screen. It is not part of the circle of working screens, and the panel never opens it by itself.

::: {.anatomy fig="five-home-alt"}
1. **Seeding rate.** In seeds per metre.
2. **Travel speed.** In km/h; yellow while it is simulated. Touch and hold it for the context menu of the speed sensor. [Speed](indicators.md#speed)
3. **Settings symbol.** A tap opens the main menu.
4. **GPS symbol.** A tap opens the GPS screen. [GPS](gps.md)
5. **Red chevrons.** A tap takes the outermost motor on that side **out of** control.
6. **Green chevrons.** A tap takes the next motor towards that side back **into** control.
7. **Target rate.** Shown in the “Precise” mode. Touch and hold it until it lights up, then swipe up or down to change it.
8. **Motor tiles.** Number and value of each motor; the icon alternates with the state sign — **STOP**, or a red × with **XXX**. Touch and hold a tile for its context menu.
9. **Stop symbol.** Touch and hold it to lock or unlock product application. A short beep confirms.

The second home screen of a machine with dispenser motors, standing still.
:::

On a machine with a fan, a pressure sensor or a pump, the **unit value** stands at the left of the top line — one at a time. A tap shows the next one; touch and hold opens its context menu.

Each motor icon **alternates**, about once a second, between the picture of the motor and the sign of its state. What the states mean: [Motors screen](motors-screen.md#reading-a-tile).

The chevrons are always on this screen. On a machine without dispenser motors they have nothing to act on.

## What you can do here

| **To do this** | **Do this** |
| --- | --- |
| Open the main menu | Tap the settings symbol |
| Change the seeding rate | Touch and hold the rate, then swipe up or down. It stays within the permitted limits. A tap elsewhere ends it. |
| Set the target of a product by weight | Touch and hold its kg/ha tile; type the rate on the number pad |
| Take motors out of or into control | Tap the red or green chevrons. Confirm with **“Yes”** if the panel asks. |
| Open the settings of a motor | Touch and hold the motor tile |
| Lock or unlock product application | Touch and hold the stop symbol. A short beep confirms. |
| See the receiver's data | Tap the GPS symbol |
| Return to the home screen | Long swipe left |

> **NOTE**
>
> **Taking a motor out of control is the same as on the Motors screen** — a motor out of control is neither driven nor watched. See [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).


# The working screens and how to move between them

The panel has **four working screens in a circle**, and a fifth that stands apart.

| **Screen** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- |
| [Home screen](home-screen.md) | The diagrams of the sections, the indicators of the devices, the speed, the area and the rates. The panel starts here. |
| [Table](table-screen.md) | The readings of every section in figures, as a list. Several tables, depending on the control mode. |
| [Statistics](statistics-screen.md) | The results of the work by field: area, path, quantities, quality. |
| [Motors](motors-screen.md) | The dispenser electric motors, and the tramline actuators if the machine has them. Present only if the profile holds at least one motor or tramline actuator. |
| [Second home screen](second-home-screen.md) | Large figures and the motor tiles. Outside the circle. |

## The circle

A **long swipe to the left** — one finger, across more than a third of the screen — moves to the next screen, always in the same direction, and returns to the home screen from the last one:

**Home screen → Table → Statistics → Motors → Home screen.**

Without motors and tramline actuators in the profile, there is no Motors screen and Statistics returns straight to the home screen.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Table and Statistics have no way back.** A swipe to the right does nothing there, and neither does a three-finger tap. To return to the home screen, keep swiping left: from the Table through Statistics (and Motors) to the home screen.

## Every way from one screen to another

| **From** | **Gesture** | **To** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home screen | Long swipe left | Table |
| Home screen | Long swipe **right** | Second home screen |
| Table | Long swipe left | Statistics |
| Statistics | Long swipe left | Motors (home screen, if the machine has none) |
| Motors | Long swipe left | Home screen |
| Motors | Long swipe right | Statistics |
| Second home screen | Long swipe left | Home screen |

A short swipe is not taken as a move to another screen; on Table and Statistics a short swipe up or down scrolls instead.

## Gestures on the working screens

| **Screen** | **What it does** | **Gesture** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home screen | Opens the main menu | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Home screen | Sets the alarm level from the real rate | **Double tap** with one finger, while applying |
| Table | Scrolls the rows | Swipe up or down |
| Table | Next or previous table | **Long** swipe right or left with **two fingers** |
| Table | Asks whether to zero the readings | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Statistics | Scrolls the report, one line per swipe | Swipe up or down |
| Statistics | Shows another field | Swipe right or left with **two fingers** |
| Statistics | Opens the menu of the screen | Tap with **two fingers** |
| Motors | Opens the context menu of a motor | Touch and hold its tile |

The full list per screen, menus and windows included: [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).


# The Table screen

The Table screen shows the readings of every section as figures, one line per section. It answers the question the diagram cannot: *which section exactly, and by how much.* Open it from the home screen with a **long swipe to the left**. It has no way back: a further long swipe left takes you on to the Statistics screen and round the circle to the home screen ([Working screens](working-screens.md)).

## A planter in the “Precise” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="five-table-precise"}
1. **#.** The number of the section.
2. **sds/m.** Seeds per metre, measured now.
3. **Q.%.** Quality — the share of seeds placed singly, as intended.
4. **Db%.** Doubles — two seeds where one was intended.
5. **Sk%.** Skips — a gap where a seed was intended.
6. **ks/Ha.** The applied rate in thousands of seeds per hectare (in the second table: seeds per metre).
7. **%.** The deviation of this section from the rate that was set.
8. **Table number.** This table and how many there are, in the corner. Shown only when there is more than one.
9. **Section number on yellow.** Something in this line has drifted towards its limit.
10. **Value on yellow.** The figure that drifted.
11. **Totals.** The same columns for the whole machine.

The first of three tables of an eight-row planter, while seeding.
:::

A value on **yellow** is drifting towards its limit; on **red** it is beyond it. A whole line in **grey** with **!** is a section taken out of control; a line in **red** with **×** is a sensor that does not answer, with **?** a device of the wrong kind.

> **NOTE**
>
> **Read the deviation column first.** A section 20 % below the others has a problem the average will not show — a partly blocked outlet, a worn disk, a sensor that needs cleaning.

## A drill in the “Flow” mode

::: {.anatomy fig="five-table-flow"}
1. **#.** The number of the section.
2. **sds/s.** Seeds per second. Dashes while nothing is counted.
3. **Deviation scale.** From −50 % through 0 to +50 %.
4. **Deviation bar.** How far this section stands from the rate that was set.
5. **%.** The same deviation as a figure.
6. **Table number.** Here table 1 of 2 — the second holds the fertilizer sections.
7. **Lowest deviation.** The section furthest below the rate.
8. **Highest deviation.** The section furthest above the rate.
9. **Recalculation interval.** The stretch over which the figures are gathered — **“Recalculation,m”** of the sensors.

The seed table of a drill with seed and fertilizer rows, standing still.
:::

## Which tables your machine has

| **Table** | **Shown when** |
| --- | --- |
| **Seed counters** — seeds per second or per metre, with the deviation bars | Always. |
| **Rate per area** (thousands per hectare) and **rate per distance** (seeds per metre) | Only in the **“Precise”** seeding control mode. |
| **Dry fertilizer** | The machine has fertilizer sensors and the fertilizer control mode is not “Precise”. |
| **Liquid fertilizer** | The machine has liquid fertilizer sensors. |

In the “Precise” mode a planter has three seed tables: rate per area (1/3), rate per distance (2/3), and the seed counters (3/3) — the count of seeds each section has sown, beside the deviation bars, with the total for the machine at the bottom.

![The seed counter table: seeds per section, deviation bars, total.](figures/five-table-counters)

## Working with the screen

| **What you want** | **Gesture** |
| --- | --- |
| Next or previous table | **Long** swipe right or left with **two fingers** |
| Scroll the lines | Swipe up or down |
| Zero the readings | Tap with **two fingers** — [Zero the readings](zero-the-readings.md) |
| Go on to Statistics | Long swipe left |

On large machines the rows do not fit on one page: swipe up and down to scroll them. A line that drifts turns yellow while you watch.


# The Statistics screen

The Statistics screen is the report of the work: how far you drove, how much you covered, how much you sowed, and how evenly. It is kept **separately for each of five fields** and survives switching off. Open it from the Table screen with a **long swipe to the left**. It has no way back: a further long swipe left goes on to the Motors screen, or to the home screen on a machine without motors.

The report is one long list. **Swipe up or down** to scroll it, one line per swipe.

## The head and the work on the field

::: {.anatomy fig="five-stat-head"}
1. **Field number.** **Field #** and the number of the field whose report you see. A **two-finger swipe** right or left shows the next or the previous field.
2. **(A).** This is the active field — the one the panel writes to now.
3. **Date and time.** Today's date and the time of day.
4. **Path.** Distance driven, in **km**.
5. **Area.** Area covered, in **Ha**.
6. **Operating time.** Hours, minutes and seconds of work.
7. **Movement speed.** The average travel speed.
8. **Started / Ended.** When the work on this field began and ended.
9. **Seeding.** The next block — see below.

The head of the report of an eight-row planter in the “Precise” mode.
:::

## The seeding block

::: {.anatomy fig="five-stat-seeding"}
1. **“Seeds sown (x1000)”.** The total, in thousands of seeds.
2. **“Quality”.** The share of seeds placed singly, as intended. Judge the work by this number.
3. **“Doubles”.** Two seeds where one was intended.
4. **“Skips”.** A gap where a seed was intended.
5. **“Not sown”.** The share of the run when nothing came out at all.
6. **“Factical” / “Setuped”.** The two column headings: what was actually applied, and what was set.
7. **“Population,ks/Ha”.** In thousands of seeds per hectare; the deviation in brackets.
8. **“Rate, s/m”.** In seeds per metre; the target on the right.
9. **“Sown” / “Not sown” / “Unknown”.** The field split three ways, in hectares.
10. **Bar.** The same split as a coloured bar: green sown, red not sown, grey unknown.
11. **“Seed sensors”.** The next block — section by section.
:::

**“Unknown”** is the area driven while the panel could not judge — not a fault, but not proof of work either.

> **NOTE**
>
> **A large deviation is not always a fault of the machine.** Before changing anything on the drill, check that the speed the panel sees matches the real one — a wrong speed moves every rate figure with it.

## Section by section

::: {.anatomy fig="five-stat-sensors"}
1. **“Seed sensors”.** One block per section follows.
2. **Section.** The section number, and the seeds it counted.
3. **q d s n.** Quality, doubles, skips and not sown for this section, in per cent.
4. **Sown / not sown / unknown.** The share of each for this section, and the bar.
5. **Population.** Thousands per hectare for this section, with its deviation.
6. **Spacing.** Seeds per metre for this section, with its deviation.
:::

This is where an uneven drill shows itself. A section with a lower quality than the rest, or a longer red part of its bar, points at that row: a blocked outlet, a worn disk, a sensor that needs cleaning.

## Blocks that appear on other machines

| **Block** | **What it holds** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Work without alarms control”** | The part of the work the panel was **not** watching — driven with the control switched off or locked. |
| **“Speed control”** | How far and how long you drove outside the permitted speed range. |
| **“Fertilizing”**, liquid fertilizer | Fertilized / not fertilized / unknown, if the machine applies them. |
| **Product** | For a product applied by weight: the quantity applied, and the actual against the set rate in kg/ha, on the line **Factical: … Setuped: …**. |

## The menu of the screen

Tap the screen with **two fingers**.

![The menu of the Statistics screen.](figures/five-stat-menu)

| **Item** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Select field”** | Makes the field shown the active one — the panel writes to it from now on. Shown only while you look at a field that is not active. If that field was worked with a different set of products by weight, the panel asks to erase its data first. |
| **“Statistics”** | Switches the report between **“Short”** and **“Full”**. Not shown on a machine without a speed sensor. |
| **“Mileage”** | Path in km and area in ha over the whole life of the system. These totals cannot be reset. Without a speed sensor, the accumulated running time instead. |
| **“Save to SD-card”** | Writes one field, or all of them, to the memory card. Shown while a card is ready. |
| **“Zero statistics”** | Erases the statistics of the field. At the Operator level the panel asks for the PIN of a higher level first; above Operator it asks **“Are you sure?”**. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The statistics are also erased by something else.** Changing the seeding control mode to or from “Precise”, or changing **“Width, cm”**, asks for confirmation and, if you confirm, **erases the statistics of every field**. Save what you need to the memory card first.


# The Motors screen

The Motors screen shows the dispenser electric motors of the machine, one tile each, and the tramline actuators if the machine has any. Look here when a row stops sowing and you want to know whether the motor is the reason.

It exists on any machine whose profile holds **at least one electric motor or one tramline actuator**. Reach it from the Statistics screen with a **long swipe to the left**. Leave it with a **long swipe to the left** to the home screen, or a **long swipe to the right** back to Statistics.

::: {.anatomy fig="five-motors"}
1. **Motor 1, STOP.** Yellow, blinking — the motor is serviceable, but product application is not running.
2. **Value of motor 1.** The driven shaft speed in rpm.
3. **Motor 2, red ×.** No connection to this motor.
4. **XXX.** No value, because the motor does not answer.

The Motors screen of a machine with two dispenser motors and no tramline actuators.
:::

## Reading a tile

The colour of the symbol is the state. The value beside it is the driven shaft speed in rpm. On the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md) the same tiles show, in the **“Precise”** control mode, the seeds per metre measured by the seed sensor of that row.

| **Symbol** | **Value** | **State** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motor, **green** | the figure | Normal. The motor is under control and driven. |
| **STOP**, yellow, blinking against the motor | the figure | The motor is serviceable, but **product application is switched off**. Nothing is wrong with it — the system is simply not applying. |
| Motor, **red** | the figure | The motor is in an alarm state. Read the alarm for the reason. |
| **×**, red | **XXX** | **No connection.** Check the cable and the connector first. |
| **!**, outlined | **!!!** | The motor is **taken out of control**. It is neither driven nor watched. |

> **NOTE**
>
> **Yellow is not a fault.** A screen full of yellow STOP signs means application is off — at the headland, or locked by hand. Red is a fault; yellow is a state you chose.

## Tramline actuators

| **Actuator symbol** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **green** | The actuator has reached its position. |
| Pulled in or pulled out, **yellow** | The actuator is moving to that position. |
| Alternating between in and out, **yellow** | The panel cannot tell the actuator's position. |
| Blinking **red** | The actuator is in an alarm state. |
| Blinking **red ×** or **?** | No connection, or a device of the wrong kind. |
| Blinking **white** | The actuator is taken out of control. |

## Working with the screen

| **What you want** | **Gesture** |
| --- | --- |
| The settings of one motor or actuator | Touch and hold its tile |
| Back to the Statistics screen | Long swipe right |
| On to the home screen | Long swipe left |

The touch and hold opens the context menu of the motor you pressed. Its **“Information”** item shows the motor's state, and for a controller fault the code of the last fault. Here you see every motor of the machine at once and can choose the one that misbehaves.


# Change the target rate

The rate field at the right end of each diagram shows two numbers: **the measured rate on top, the target below it**. In the “Flow” mode the target is the alarm level of the diagram — see [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).

## On a diagram

::: steps
1. On the home screen, **touch and hold the diagram** whose rate you want to change, for more than half a second. Its target figure lights up.

   ![The seed diagram with its target figure lit for editing.](figures/five-home-highlight)

2. **Swipe up** over the screen to raise the target, **down** to lower it — one step per swipe. The target stays within its permitted limits.

3. **Tap the screen outside the diagrams** to finish. The figure stops being lit and the new target is in force.
:::

To change another diagram — fertilizer after seed, say — touch and hold that diagram instead.

## For a product applied by weight

::: steps
1. Touch and hold the kg/ha indicator of the product. The number pad opens with the caption **Product** and the number of the product.

2. Type the target, from 10.0 to 500.0 kg/ha, and touch **“OK”** ([Entering numbers](interface-basics.md#entering-numbers)). A tap outside the pad leaves the target as it was.
:::

## On the second home screen

Touch and hold the rate until it lights up, then swipe up or down. A tap elsewhere ends it. See [Second home screen](second-home-screen.md).

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Columns under the line are not guarded.** If the target is set far above what the machine really delivers, the columns sink under the control line and the panel shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. On a grain drill, let the panel find the level: [Set the alarm level automatically](set-the-alarm-level.md).


# Lock product application by hand

The manual lock stops **all product application**: the dispenser motors and the pump do not run, however the machine moves. Use it to cross a field already sown, to drive on the road with the implement lowered, or when you work [without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).

The lock exists on machines with **dispenser electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump**.

::: steps
1. On the home screen, **touch and hold an empty place in the right-hand column** of indicators — not on an icon — until the panel beeps once.

2. Check the right-hand column. A **yellow hand** blinks there: application is locked.

   ![The right-hand column of the home screen with the yellow hand.](figures/five-home-lock)

3. To unlock, touch and hold the same place again. One short beep; the hand disappears.
:::

A touch and hold **on an icon** of the column opens the context menu of that device instead.

On the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md), touch and hold the **stop symbol** — the same lock, the same beep.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The lock is announced by the screen only.** Look for the yellow hand before you start a pass. A locked machine drives a whole field and sows nothing.

## What the lock changes elsewhere

- The motor tiles on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md) show a yellow **STOP** — serviceable, not applying.
- The product application control does not start when you move off — the lock must be off for the control to start ([Quick start](quick-start.md#moving-off)).
- The work done while locked is counted in the statistics as **“Work without alarms control”** ([Statistics](statistics-screen.md)).

## When the panel locks by itself

Switching speed imitation on locks product application. A panel that is switched on with imitation already on starts locked as well. Unlock by hand when you are ready to apply: [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).


# Set the alarm level automatically

On a grain drill the seeds arrive too close together to be counted one by one, so the panel guards each row against an **alarm level**: the line on the diagram. Set it too high and every row sinks under the line — **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”**. Set it too low and a half-blocked row goes unnoticed. The panel can set it for you from what the machine really sows.

This works in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes, for the seed and the dry fertilizer diagrams, and for liquid fertilizer in the “Flow” mode. In the “Precise” mode the double tap changes nothing.

::: steps
1. Start seeding at your normal speed, with product flowing through every row.

2. **Double tap** the home screen with one finger — two quick taps on the same place.

3. The panel beeps once and lights the rate field: the new alarm level is set from the rate being sown now — **half** of it in the “Flow” mode, **one tenth** of it in the “Hybrid” mode.

   ![The diagrams after the double tap: the columns above the line, the rate field lit.](figures/five-home-auto-level)

4. Check that every column stands above its line. The light goes out by itself after a few seconds.
:::

The double tap works only while product is being applied. Standing still, nothing happens.

> **TIP**
>
> **Repeat it after a change of seed lot or speed.** The level follows the rate at the moment of the tap. You can also correct it by hand: touch and hold the diagram, then swipe up or down — see [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md).

What the line means and why rows under it are not watched: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md#the-line-rows-under-it-are-not-under-control).


# Take a sensor into or out of control

A sensor **out of control** is not watched: the panel raises no alarm about it, whatever it reports. Take a sensor out of control when its section is out of work on purpose or when the sensor is broken and you must finish the field. Take it back as soon as you can.

## Take a sensor out of control

::: steps
1. On the home screen, **touch and hold** the sensor — its column on the diagram, or its icon. Its context menu opens.

   ![The context menu of a seed sensor.](figures/five-ctx-seed)

2. Tap **“Disable control”** to select it, and tap it again.

3. The first time in a session, the panel asks **“Are you sure that you want disable control?”**. Touch **“Yes”**. A touch outside the window cancels.

   ![The question before control is switched off.](figures/five-question-disable-control)

4. The column turns white with **!** (an icon alternates with a white [!]). The sensor is no longer watched.
:::

## Take it back into control

Do the same and choose **“Enable control”**. The first time in a session the panel asks **“Are you sure that you want enable control?”**; confirm with **“Yes”**. A seed sensor taken back into control shows a yellow **?** for a few seconds while it receives its settings.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A switched-off sensor is blind, not quiet.** Nothing about it is reported, however wrong it goes.

## When the statistics must be erased

For some sensors the panel first asks to erase the statistics of the active field: it says **“Need to erase data, for selected field!”** and asks again.

- **“Yes”** erases the statistics of the active field and changes the control. At the Operator level the panel first asks for the PIN of a higher level; a wrong PIN shows **“Invalid PIN”** and nothing changes.
- **“No”** leaves both as they are.

The speed sensor cannot be taken out of control — its context menu has no such item. Motors are taken out of control the same way, from their tile on the [Motors screen](motors-screen.md), or with the chevrons on the [second home screen](second-home-screen.md). What the four combinations of control and product application mean: [The four states of a section](section-states.md#the-four-states-of-a-section).


# Zero the readings of the Table screen

The Table screen keeps counting from the moment its readings were last zeroed. Zero them when you start a new field or a new seed lot, so that the counters and deviations describe only the new work.

::: steps
1. Open the Table screen: a **long swipe to the left** on the home screen.

2. Tap the screen with **two fingers**. The panel asks **“Zero readings?”**.

   ![The question before zeroing: Yes in green, No in red.](figures/five-question-zero-readings)

3. Touch **“Yes”**. The counters of every seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer sensor are set to zero.
:::

**“No”**, or a touch outside the window, leaves everything as it was.

To get back to the home screen afterwards, keep swiping left — through Statistics (and Motors) to the home screen. The Table screen has no way back ([Working screens](working-screens.md)).

**Only the counters of the Table screen are zeroed.** The [field statistics](statistics-screen.md) are not touched; they are erased with **“Zero statistics”** in the menu of the Statistics screen.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Zeroing cannot be undone.** Do it when you start something new, not to tidy the screen.


# Fill the disks with seeds

This applies only to planters with seed **dispenser electric motors** in the **“Precise”** control mode. Without motors in the profile, or in another mode, the menu item is not shown.

When the disks are driven by electric motors, they stand empty until the motors run. Drive off with empty disks and the first metres of every row get nothing: each disk has to pick up seeds and carry them round to the drop point first. Filling turns the disks while the machine stands still, so that sowing starts from the first metre.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The disks turn while the machine stands still.** Before you start, make sure nobody is near the metering units, the dispenser shafts or the drive. The disks start together and each keeps turning for up to about twenty seconds. From the cab the metering units cannot be seen.

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. The item is shown only while the machine **stands still**.

2. On the home screen, tap with **two fingers**. The main menu opens with **“Fill the disks with seeds”** already selected; tap it once more.

   ![The main menu with Fill the disks with seeds selected.](figures/five-main-menu)

3. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”**. Touch **“Yes”**. **“No”**, or a touch outside the window, cancels.

   ![The question before the disks turn.](figures/five-fill-confirm)

4. Watch the tiles. Each motor turns its disk until the seed sensor of its row registers the first seed. At the end the panel beeps three times and shows **“Operation complete.”**

5. Touch **“Close”** to return to the home screen.
:::

To stop before the end, touch **“Cancel”**: the motors stop at once and go back to the seeding control.

## Reading the screen

::: {.anatomy fig="five-fill-screen"}
1. **Green tile.** Done: the seed sensor registered a seed, the disk is filled.
2. **Dark red tile.** Failed: the disk could not be filled. The motor number is bright red.
3. **Reason letters.** Why the tile failed — see the table below.
4. **“Operation complete.”** Every motor has finished.
5. **“Close”.** Returns to the home screen. While the operation runs, this button reads **“Cancel”**.

The end of the operation on an eight-motor planter.
:::

| **Tile** | **State** |
| --- | --- |
| Dark grey | Waiting its turn. Up to eight motors run at the same time; the rest wait. |
| Yellow | Running: the disk is turning. |
| Green | Done. |
| Dark red | Failed. |

Each motor turns its disk at **4 rpm of the driven shaft**. If no seed is registered within **1.25 revolutions — about 19 seconds** — that motor is stopped and marked as failed. A motor already in an alarm state is marked as failed at once. With the fertilizer control mode also in “Precise”, the fertilizer motors are run the same way.

> **NOTE**
>
> **While the disks are being filled, alarm windows are held back.** The panel raises its access level for the duration of the operation and returns to your level at the end.

## Letters on a failed tile

The colour of the letter matters as much as the letter: **red means a fault, white means taken out of control.**

| **Letter** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **m** red | A fault of the dispenser electric motor during the operation. |
| **m** white | The motor is taken out of control and cannot run. |
| **g** red | The seed sensor registered no seed while the disk was turning. |
| **s** red | A fault of the seed sensor during the operation. |
| **s** white | The seed sensor is taken out of control. |

If the **seed sensor** is out of control, the panel cannot check the disk. A serviceable motor still turns it for about one and a quarter turns, so in practice the disk does get filled — but the panel reports that motor as failed, because it never saw a seed.


# Set up the tramline rhythm

A **tramline** is the lane the sprayer will drive in later. You make it now, while sowing, by shutting off one or two sections on certain bouts so that nothing is sown where the sprayer wheels will go. Which bouts those are depends on the width of the drill against the width of the sprayer. That pattern, repeating across the field, is the **rhythm**.

## How a rhythm works — an example

A 6-metre drill and an 18-metre sprayer: every third bout must carry the lane. The rhythm is three bouts long, and actuator 1 shuts its sections off on one of them.

| **Bout** | **Actuator 1** | **What is sown** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | shuts its sections off | All rows except the tramline rows — the lane is made. |
| 2 | open | All rows. |
| 3 | open | All rows. |
| 1 again | shuts off | The next lane, 18 m further. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Get the rhythm wrong and the field looks perfect until the sprayer arrives and has nowhere to drive.** Check the bout count against the sprayer, not against the drill.

## What the panel allows

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Rhythms stored** | **Three.** One is active at a time. |
| **Actuators in one rhythm** | **Four.** On a machine that makes tramlines by stopping dispenser motors, the motors take their place. |
| **Cut-off bouts per actuator** | **Four** different bouts of the same rhythm. |
| **Bouts in a rhythm** | 1 to 50. |

## Setting it up

The tramline items sit under **“Seeding machine parameters”**, which needs the **Agronomist** level: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md). The **“Tramline”** item is shown only on a machine that can make tramlines.

::: steps
1. On the home screen tap with **two fingers**. Tap **“Settings”**, and tap it again.

2. Tap **“Seeding machine parameters”**, and tap it again.

3. Tap **“Tramline”**, and tap it again.

   ![The Tramline menu.](figures/five-menu-tramline)

4. Tap **“Tramline”** and swipe right to **“Yes”**. Then tap **“Tramline rhythm settings”** twice. The rhythm form opens with rhythm 1 selected.

5. On **“Rhythm”**, swipe right or left to choose the rhythm number. Tap with **two fingers** and choose **“Select”**. The word **“Active”** appears beside the number — without it the rhythm is stored but not used.

6. Swipe down to **“Bouts”**, tap with two fingers and set the number of bouts in the rhythm.

7. Swipe to the framed cell under the activation heading and tap with two fingers. Choose the number of the actuator, then the **bout** on which it must shut its sections off.

8. If the pattern needs it, add more bouts to the same actuator — up to four — with the framed cell at the end of its row, or another actuator with the cell on the empty row below.

9. Tap with **three fingers**. The rhythm is saved and the Tramline menu returns. Tap outside the menus until the home screen returns. The tramline indicator shows the current bout and the number of bouts.
:::

A touch and hold anywhere on the form saves the rhythm without leaving it. Return to the **Operator** level before you work — above it, no alarms are shown.

## The rhythm form

::: {.anatomy fig="five-tramline-rhythm-form"}
1. **“Rhythm”.** The number of the rhythm; a swipe right or left steps through the three.
2. **“Active”.** This rhythm is the one in use.
3. **“Bouts”.** The number of bouts in the rhythm.
4. **Activation heading.** **“Tramline actuators activation”** on a machine that makes tramlines with actuators; **“Tramline motors activation”** on one that stops dispenser motors. A machine with both shows both headings.
5. **Framed cell.** Adds an actuator (or motor) and its cut-off bout.

A new rhythm: one bout, nothing shut off yet.
:::

In the form, a swipe up or down moves between lines, a swipe right or left along a line, and a **two-finger tap** opens the selected cell. **“Reset rhythm settings”**, in the menu of the **“Rhythm”** line, returns the selected rhythm to its defaults.

## How the bout changes

The panel counts the bouts by itself. Something on the machine must tell it that a pass has ended:

| **On the machine** | **What ends a bout** |
| --- | --- |
| Marker sensors in the profile | At least one marker sensor **under control** and **answering**. The change of the marker position ends the bout. |
| No markers | The **work position sensor**, under control and answering. Raising the implement out of work ends the bout. |
| Neither | The bout does not change. |

When the bout cannot change by itself, the tramline icon on the home screen is **yellow** ([Tramline bout](indicators.md#tramline-bout)). Check the indicator on the home screen before you start a pass.


# Set the screen brightness

::: steps
1. On the home screen tap with **two fingers**. Tap **“Settings”**, and tap it again.
