2. **“Brightness,%”** is the first item. Tap it, then swipe right to brighten or left to dim, in steps of 10, from 0 to 100.

   ![The Settings menu with Brightness,% selected.](figures/five-menu-settings)

3. Tap outside the menu to leave it. The new brightness stays in force and is stored by itself.
:::

There is **no automatic brightness**: the screen stays at the value you set, day and night. Dim it for night work and raise it again in the morning. **0 is the dimmest setting, not off** — the screen stays lit.

The same menu holds **“Volume”** — the loudness of the alarm sound — and **“Buttons sound”**, the click on every touch. Everything else in the Settings menu: [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).


# Work without the speed sensor

**Symptom.** The speed field shows **XX.X** in red, or the speed stays at zero although the machine moves. Without a speed, the panel cannot calculate area, rates or deviations, and the dispenser motors do not know how fast to turn.

**Cause.** The speed sensor or the device that carries it does not answer, or the wheel no longer gives pulses.

**What to do.** Two ways, both through the context menu of the speed sensor — touch and hold the speed field. Both items need the Agronomist level: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

## Take the speed from GPS

Set **“GPS internal”** to **“Yes”**. The panel takes the travel speed from its own receiver. Watch the satellite symbol in the right-hand column: green or yellow is usable, red is not. See [GPS](gps.md).

## Work on a simulated speed

> **WARNING**
>
> **With speed imitation on, the panel drives the dispenser motors and the pump as if the machine were moving** — also while it stands. Switch imitation off before you leave the cab, and lock application whenever you stop.

::: steps
1. Touch and hold the speed field. Its context menu opens.

2. Set **“Imitation, km/h”** to the speed you will drive, up to 20 km/h. The panel tells you **“Settings of Min and Max speed switched off!”** — the speed limits are not watched while the speed is simulated.

3. The panel locks product application by itself: the yellow hand appears in the right-hand column.

4. Return to the **Operator** level, so that alarms are shown again.

5. The speed field now shows a yellow figure alternating with **“IMITATION”** ([Speed](indicators.md#speed)).

6. Control the application with the **manual lock**: touch and hold an empty place of the right-hand column to start applying on a pass, and again to stop at the headland. See [Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md).

7. Drive at the speed you set. The rates are right only as long as the real speed matches it.
:::

When the sensor is repaired, set **“Imitation, km/h”** back to **“No”** — swipe left until the value reads **“No”** — and set the speed limits again.

> **NOTE**
>
> **A panel switched on with imitation still set starts locked.** If nothing is applied after a restart, look for the yellow hand.

Details of the speed sensor settings: [Speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).


# Access levels

Not every setting is open to everyone. The panel has three access levels. **After every power-on it starts at the lowest one, “Operator”.**

| **Level** | **What it opens** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Operator”** | Everyday work: brightness, volume, language, alarm delay, the clock, the target rates and alarm levels, taking a sensor into or out of control, the mass calibrations. Resetting the statistics asks for a PIN at this level. |
| **“Agronomist”** | The commissioning settings: **“Seeding machine parameters”**, **“Product rate error,%”**, most sensor parameters, the speed and dispenser calibrations, and the **“Service”** menu with the profile and the device configuration. Needs a PIN. |
| **“Service”** | Everything above, plus the reset-to-defaults items, **“Reset settings”**, **“Save factory defaults”**, the serial number, the trial period and **“Imitation mode”**. For the service department. Needs a PIN. |

Every settings table in this manual names the level an item needs. **An item above your level is not shown in the menu at all** — if an item named here is missing, check the level first.

## Switch the level

The level is changed in one place only: **“Settings”** → **“User”**. Going **up** a level asks for the PIN of that level; going **down** does not. Step by step: [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

Ask your dealer or the service support for the PIN.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” no alarm windows are shown.** When seeding starts at such a level, the panel warns once in a red window — see [User is Agronomist](alarms-access-level.md). Return to **“Operator”** before you work, or switch the panel off and on.

## What happens to the alarms while the level is high

The alarms are not lost while they are hidden — they wait. When you lower the level to **“Operator”**, the panel drops the ones that have gone away in the meantime and shows the ones that are **still true**, one window after another — also those you had already closed before you raised the level. After an hour of commissioning at **“Agronomist”**, expect a short run of alarm windows on the way back down. It is the backlog, not a new fault. How the windows work: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).


# Enable the Agronomist level

Most set-up work — sensor parameters, calibrations, the profile, device configuration — needs the **“Agronomist”** level. The **“Service”** level is raised the same way. What each level opens: [Access levels](access-levels.md).

You need the PIN of the level you want. A PIN opens only its own level: choose **“Agronomist”** and type the Agronomist PIN.

::: steps
1. On the home screen tap with **two fingers**. The main menu opens.

   ![The main menu.](figures/five-main-menu)

2. Tap **“Settings”**, and tap it again. The **“Settings”** menu opens.

   ![The Settings menu at the Operator level.](figures/five-menu-settings)

3. Find **“User”** near the end of the menu — swipe up if it is not in view — and tap it. Swipe right until it reads **“Agronomist”** (or **“Service”**).

   ![“User” set to Agronomist.](figures/five-menu-user-agronomist)

4. Tap **“User”** again. The number pad opens with **“Enter your PIN:”**. Type the PIN and tap **“OK”**.

   ![The number pad asking for the PIN.](figures/five-pin-pad)

5. A short window names the new level, and the **“Settings”** menu returns with the items of that level — for example **“Seeding machine parameters”**. Tap outside the menu to leave.
:::

A wrong PIN shows **“Invalid PIN”** in a red window, and the number pad opens again. To give up, tap outside the number pad; the level stays as it was.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **At “Agronomist” and “Service” no alarm windows are shown.** When you have finished, return to **“Operator”**: repeat steps 1–3, swipe left to **“Operator”** and tap **“User”** again — no PIN is asked going down. Switching the panel off and on does the same.

When you come back down, the alarms that are still true are shown one after another. See [Access levels](access-levels.md#what-happens-to-the-alarms-while-the-level-is-high).


# The profile

The profile tells the panel **which devices, and how many of each**, are on the machine. A panel usually arrives with the profile already set. **Check it before you set anything else**: a device missing from the profile is never watched, and a device in the profile that is not fitted raises **“Connection lost”**.

## Check the profile on the home screen

Switch the panel on and wait until the home screen appears. Then look at it:

- **No “Connection lost” alarm** — the panel has found every device the profile declares.
- **No white indicators with an exclamation mark** — no device is left out of control.
- **No red indicators with an “X”** — every device answers.

What the indicators mean: [Indicators](indicators.md). How to take a device into control or out of it: [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> A profile is sometimes supplied with devices that are **not in the delivery**, so that the system can be extended later. Those indicators stay out of control on purpose. Do not switch their control on.

## Open the profile

The profile needs the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). Tap the home screen with two fingers, then tap **“Service”** twice and **“Profile”** twice. Change the selected item with a swipe right or left.

![The top of the Profile menu.](figures/five-menu-profile)

## The profile items

| **Item** | **Range** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Seed sensors”** | **2 … 120.** The menu lets you set 1, but such a profile is refused when it is saved. |
| **“Fertilizer sensors”** | **0 … 60**; seed and fertilizer sensors together **not more than 120**. |
| **“Liq.fert.flow sensors”** | **0 … 60** — liquid fertilizer section sensors. |
| **“Hoppers”** | 0 … 9 |
| **“Dispensers”** | 0 … 9 — dispenser shaft sensors. |
| **“Speed”** | **“No”** / **“Control panel”** (sensor wired to the panel) / **“Input device”** (one wheel sensor on an input device) / **“Input device (2)”** (two wheel sensors on an input device). |
| **“Fans”** | 0 … 2 |
| **“Pressure sensors”** | 0 … 3 |
| **“Work position sensor”** | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Markers”** | **“No”** / **“One”** / **“Both”** |
| **“No battery charge”**, **“Emergency oil pressure”**, **“Ignition”**, **“Low fuel”**, **“Air filter”** | The engine sensors — **“No”** / **“Yes”** each. |
| **“EMD of the seeds”** | **0 … 60** — seed dispenser electric motors. |
| **“EMD of the fertilizers”** | **0 … 30** — fertilizer dispenser electric motors; both motor groups together **not more than 60**. |
| **“Tramline actuators”** | 0 … 4 |
| **“Liq.fert.pump controller”** | 0 … 1 |

At the end of the menu follow **“Save settings”**, **“Load settings”**, the two memory card items and **“Save profile”** — see below and [Save and load settings](save-and-load-settings.md).

## When the panel refuses a profile

The panel checks the whole profile, not only the item you changed. It refuses a profile when:

- the hopper, dispenser and engine sensors together come to **more than 12**;
- they come to **more than 10** while the pressure and fan sensors together come to more than four;
- the pressure and fan sensors together come to **more than five**;
- there are **fertilizer motors but no seed motors**, or fertilizer motors but no fertilizer sensors;
- there are electric motors or a liquid fertilizer pump **but no speed sensor**.

## Save the profile

::: steps
1. After changing the profile, tap **“Save profile”** at the end of the menu, and tap it again.

2. If nothing was changed, the panel shows **“No changes”**. If the profile breaks one of the rules above, it shows **“Invalid profile!”** in red and saves nothing. Otherwise it asks **“Are you sure?”**.

   ![The question before the profile is saved.](figures/five-confirm-sure)

3. Tap **“Yes”**. The panel shows **“Wait...”**, then **“Saved”** and **“Restart system”**, and restarts by itself.
:::

A tap on **“No”**, or outside the question window, leaves the saved profile as it was.


# Save and load settings

The panel can **keep a copy of its settings** and bring it back later — useful before you try something out. With a memory card in the slot it can also **write the profile to the card**. All these items are at the end of the **“Profile”** menu ([The profile](profile.md)) and need the **“Agronomist”** level.

| **Item in the “Profile” menu** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Save settings”** | Keeps a copy of the current settings inside the panel. |
| **“Load settings”** | Brings that copy back. |
| **“Save to SD-card”** | Writes the profile to the memory card. Shown only while a card is in the slot and ready. |
| **“Load from SD-card”** | Shows the list of the profiles on the card. Shown only while a card is ready. |
| **“Save factory defaults”** | Stores the current settings as the factory values. **“Service”** level only. |

## Keep and restore the settings

::: steps
1. Raise the level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)), tap the home screen with two fingers and open **“Service”** → **“Profile”** — tap each item twice.

2. Swipe up to the end of the menu. Tap **“Save settings”** or **“Load settings”**, and tap it again. The panel asks **“Are you sure?”**.

   ![The question before the settings are saved.](figures/five-confirm-sure)

3. Tap **“Yes”**. The panel answers **“Saved”** or **“Loaded”**.

   ![The panel confirms with “Saved”.](figures/five-info-saved)
:::

If there is no copy to bring back, **“Load settings”** ends with **“FAILURE”** in a red window.

## Write the profile to the memory card

Tap **“Save to SD-card”** twice. There is no question: the panel writes the profile and answers **“Saved”**. If the card cannot be written, it answers **“FAILURE”**; if the card has gone, **“FAILURE”** and **“Insert SD-card”**.

- The files are named automatically, **P0001.pfl** and onwards, in the **PROFILES** folder of the card.
- Keep the card for its own panel: a profile file written by one firmware version is very likely **not readable** by another.

## The list of profiles on the card

**“Load from SD-card”** opens a list of the profile files found on the card. A file the panel cannot read is shown in **red**. A tap with **three fingers** closes the list. With no profile files on the card, the item answers **“FAILURE”**.


# The Settings menu

The **“Settings”** menu holds the settings of the panel itself. Open it from the home screen: tap with **two fingers**, then tap **“Settings”** twice. The settings of the individual sensors are elsewhere — see [Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md).

::: {.anatomy fig="five-menu-settings"}
1. **“Brightness,%”** — the backlight. The selected item shows its value between **-** and **+**; swipe right or left to change it.
2. **“Volume”** — the loudness of the alarm sound.
3. **“Language”** — the language of the screens.
4. **“Buttons sound”** — a click on every touch the screen takes.
5. **“Seeding diagram settings”** — how the seed diagram is drawn. [Below](#diagram-settings).
6. **“Change Date&Time”** — the clock. [Below](#change-date-and-time).
7. **“Alarm delay”** — how long a fault must last before the alarm window opens.
8. **“User”** — the access level. [Access levels](access-levels.md).

The **“Settings”** menu of a planter with a speed sensor in the **“Precise”** mode, at the **“Operator”** level, with **“Brightness,%”** selected.
:::

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The menu does not always have the same items.** The access level, the machine in the profile and the modes of the diagrams change it. If an item named here is missing, check those three before looking for a fault.

## The items

| **Item** | **Range and default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Brightness,%”** | 0 … 100, in steps of 10; default 100. 0 is the dimmest setting, not off. See [Screen brightness](screen-brightness.md). | Operator |
| **“Volume”** | 0 … 100, in steps of 10; default 100. | Operator |
| **“Language”** | English, Ukrainian, Polish, Hungarian, Romanian, Bulgarian. | Operator |
| **“Buttons sound”** | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; default **“Yes”**. | Operator |
| **“Seeding diagram settings”**, **“Fertil. diagram settings”**, **“Liq.fert. diagram settings”** | Submenus. Each is shown only when the machine has a speed sensor, its own sensors are in the profile and its diagram is **not** in the **“Flow”** mode. | Operator |
| **“Change Date&Time”** | Submenu. | Operator |
| **“Alarm delay”** | **2 … 20 s**; default 3 s. See [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). | Operator |
| **“Product rate error,%”** | **3 … 20 %**; default 5 %. How far a product dosed by weight, or the liquid fertilizer pump, may stand from its target before an alarm. Shown only when a product is dosed by weight or a pump controller is in the profile. | Agronomist |
| **“Seeding machine parameters”** | Submenu: width, modes, tramline, calibrations. Hidden when the machine has neither a speed sensor nor a tramline actuator. [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md) | Agronomist |
| **“User”** | **“Operator”** / **“Agronomist”** / **“Service”**. [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md) | Operator |
| **“Reset settings”** | Returns the settings to the factory values. | Service |

On a machine with two groups of seed sensors, the two diagram items read **“Seeding gr.A diagram”** and **“Seeding gr.B diagram”**.

**The settings are stored by themselves** a few seconds after the last change. Wait a moment before you switch the panel off.

## Diagram settings

![The diagram settings of the seed sensors.](figures/five-menu-diagram)

There are three of these menus — seed, dry fertilizer, liquid fertilizer. The liquid fertilizer menu has only **“Grid”** and **“Reset to defaults”**.

| **Item** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Skips & Doubles”** | **“Yes”** shows the skip and double bars over the last stretch of the path. **“Precise” mode only.** Default **“Yes”**. |
| **“Grid”** | **“No”** — only the rate line; **“Partial”** — only the tolerance limits; **“Full”** — both. Default **“Full”**. |
| **“Scale S&D,%”** | The height of the skip and double bars, **5 … 50 %** in steps of 5; default 20. **“Precise” mode only.** |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Returns this menu to the factory values. **Service** level only. |

## Change Date and Time

::: steps
1. Tap **“Change Date&Time”**, and tap it again. The fields **“Year”**, **“Month”**, **“Day”**, **“Hours”**, **“Minutes”** and **“Seconds”** open, with **“Set”** at the end.

   ![The date and time fields.](figures/five-menu-datetime)

2. Tap a field and swipe right or left until it shows the value you need — one step per swipe. The days follow the month.

3. Tap **“Set”**, and tap it again. The clock takes the new values and the **“Settings”** menu returns.
:::

Leaving the fields with a tap outside the menu, without **“Set”**, keeps the old time.


# Seeding machine parameters

**“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**. The item needs the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)) and is hidden on a machine with neither a speed sensor nor a tramline actuator. Which items it holds depends on the profile.

![The Seeding machine parameters menu of a planter: the width in square brackets, the two modes, the two calibrations.](figures/five-param-edit)

| **Item** | **Values** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Width, cm”** | 100 … 2500; default 560. Number pad. |
| **“Mode of seeding”** | **“Flow”** / **“Hybrid”** / **“Precise”**; default **“Flow”**. |
| **“Mode of fertilizers”** | **“Flow”** / **“Hybrid”** / **“Precise”**. |
| **“Mode of liq.fert.”** | **“Flow”** / **“By area”**. |
| **“Tramline”** | Submenu. |
| **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** | Opens the mapping screen. |
| **“Speed calibration”** | Starts the speed calibration. |
| **“Dispenser calibration”** | **“ALL”**, or the number of one dispenser; starts the rotation calibration. |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Returns the width and the modes to the factory values. **Service** level only. |

## Width, cm

The working width of the implement. The worked area is calculated from it, so it must be entered. Tap the item twice, or swipe on it: the number pad opens. Type the width and tap **“OK”**; a tap outside the pad keeps the old value. The item is hidden without a speed sensor.

If the statistics already hold work, the panel first asks to erase them — the area of the old width and of the new one cannot be added together.

## Mode of seeding, Mode of fertilizers

| **Mode** | **Unit** | **For** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Flow”** | seeds per second | grain drills |
| **“Hybrid”** | seeds per metre | grain drills |
| **“Precise”** | seeds per metre, with skips and doubles counted | precision planters |

The fertilizers can be set to **“Precise”** only while the seeding is **“Precise”**. On a machine with two groups of seed sensors the two items read **“Mode of seeding gr.A”** and **“Mode of seeding gr.B”**; group B can be **“Precise”** only while group A is, so set group B to **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”** before you take group A out of **“Precise”**.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Switching between “Precise” and the other two modes demands a reset of the statistics** if any field has work recorded in it. The panel asks first; **“No”** keeps the old mode.

## Liquid fertilizer mode

**“Flow”** (litres per minute) or **“By area”** (litres per hectare). **Shown only when there is no liquid fertilizer pump controller in the profile** — with a controller the panel works by area.

## Relation of sensors to actuators

Which section sensors belong to which tramline actuator or dispenser motor. When an actuator shuts its sections off, their sensors switch to tramline monitoring. The item is shown only where there is something to relate: tramline actuators, or dispenser motors that are not one to one with the section sensors.

![The mapping screen: one line for the actuators, one for the motors.](figures/five-mapping)

A mapping is a **range** of sections, **“Diapason start”** to **“Diapason end”** — equal numbers mean a single section. Up to **four ranges** can be attached to one actuator. On a machine with dispenser motors the screen also has **“Motors to sensors mapping”**.

On the screen, a swipe up or down moves between the lines, a swipe right or left along a line, and a **two-finger tap** opens the menu of the selected cell — to add a range or to **“Remove diapason”**. **Touch and hold** anywhere on the screen to apply the mapping.

## Tramline

A submenu with two items: **“Tramline”** (**“No”** / **“Yes”**) and **“Tramline rhythm settings”**. Shown only on a machine that can make tramlines. Setting up a rhythm: [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).

## Speed calibration and Dispenser calibration

The two calibrations that need the machine to move. Both are hidden without a speed sensor. Select **“Dispenser calibration”** and swipe right or left to choose the dispenser — or **“ALL”** for all of them at once — then tap it again to start.

- [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)
- [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md)


# Sensor settings

Every sensor, actuator and motor on the machine has its own settings and its own status screen. Both are reached through its **context menu**. The parameters of each kind of sensor are in the topics that follow this one.

## Reach a sensor

**Touch and hold the device** for more than half a second:

- on the **home screen** — its icon, or its column on a diagram;
- on the **Motors screen** or the **second home screen** — the tile of a motor or a tramline actuator.

The context menu opens. A short tap does nothing. A touch and hold on a kg/ha indicator, on the target of a diagram or on an empty place of the right-hand column does something else — see [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).

![The context menu of a fan sensor at the Agronomist level.](figures/five-ctx-fan)

## The context menu

| **Item** | **What it does** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Information”** | Opens the status screen of this device. [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md) | Operator |
| **“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”** | Takes the device out of monitoring, or back in. Not offered for the speed sensor. [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md) | Operator |
| **“Registers”** | A raw view of the device's registers, for the service department. Not part of any procedure. For a motor or the pump controller the item reads **“Electric motors”** and opens the diagnostic screen of the controllers. | Agronomist |
| The device's own items | For example **“Speed calibration”** for the speed sensor. | as stated |
| The parameters | Which ones you see depends on the access level. Change the selected one with a swipe right or left. | as stated |
| **“Reset to defaults”** | Returns this device's parameters to the factory values. | Service |

Tap outside the menu to leave it. Changed values are stored by themselves.

## The status screen

**“Information”** opens the status screen of the device: its identity, its link, its live figures and its active alarms. How to read it: [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## Calibrations

Four calibrations exist. They are not variants of one procedure: each writes different parameters and is reached a different way.

| **What it puts right** | **Where** | **Level** | **Machine** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Travel speed — rewrites **“Factor, %”** of the speed sensor. [Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md) | **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Speed calibration”**, or **“Speed calibration”** in the context menu of the speed sensor | Agronomist in the menu, Operator in the context menu | drives 100 m |
| Dispenser rotation — **“Wheel, pulses”** against **“Dispenser pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md) | **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Dispenser calibration”** | Agronomist | wheel and dispenser shaft turned together |
| Dispenser mass — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**. [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md) | context menu of the dispenser sensor | Operator | standing |
| Metering roller mass — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** of one motor. [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md) | context menu of the dispenser electric motor | Operator | standing |

The context-menu items **“Speed calibration”** and the motor calibration are offered only while the machine stands still. The two mass calibrations are at the **“Operator”** level because they have to be repeated whenever the product changes.


# The sensor status screen

Reached through **“Information”** in the context menu of a device ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). It shows what the panel knows about one device.

## The screen

::: {.anatomy fig="five-status-hopper"}
1. **“Channel #”** — which device of the whole list this is.
2. **The marks either side of the channel number.** Swipe **left** for the previous device, **right** for the next one. The screen stays open.
3. **“Address:”** — the address the device answers on. Not given in this manual.
4. **“Type:”** — the kind of device and its number, here hopper sensor 1.
5. **“Link:”** — the state of the communication. [Table below](#link-states).
6. **The figures of this kind of device** — here the level on the input of a hopper sensor. [Table below](#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).
7. **“Alarm 1 from 1”** — how many alarms of this device are active.
8. **The name of the alarm** — the first of the active alarms.

The status screen of a hopper sensor whose hopper is empty.
:::

Some devices show one more line, **“Unit:”** — the unit the device is connected to, for example **“Control panel”** for the travel speed sensor.

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Swipe right / left | Next / previous device — the screen stays open. |
| Swipe up, or three-finger tap | Back to where you came from. |

## Link states

| **State** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Normal”** | The device answers. |
| **“Not controlled”** | The device is out of control: neither the communication nor anything else is watched. |
| **“No connection”** | The device does not answer. Red. |
| **“Wrong device type!”** | Something answers, but not the kind of device the profile expects. Red. |
| **“IMITATION”** | Speed sensor only: the speed is simulated, not measured. Yellow. |

The figures are drawn only while the device is **under control**, answers, and is of the expected kind. A device out of control shows its identity and nothing else.

## What each kind of sensor adds

![The status screen of a speed sensor wired to the panel.](figures/five-status-speed)

| **Device** | **What the screen shows** |
| --- | --- |
| Speed sensor | The pulse frequency **F=** in Hz; with two speed sensors **F1=** and **F2=**. Under it the two limits **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”**. On a machine that doses a product by weight with electric motors, the limits are those the motors can hold, narrowed by the two settings; a limit the settings cannot meet is written in red as an inequality. Without such motors a limit set to zero is shown as **----**, switched off. |
| Hopper sensor | **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**. |
| Dispenser shaft sensor | **F=** in Hz, to three decimals. |
| Fan sensor | **F=** in Hz. |
| Pressure sensor | **P=** in kPa. |
| Seed sensor, dry fertilizer sensor | **Status:** and one of eight states — [below](#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor). |
| Liquid fertilizer flow sensor | **Status:** **Working**, or **Working:Tramline** in the tramline mode; under it **Flow=** in L/min. |
| Work position sensor | **“Position: Working”** or **“Position: Transporting”**, and **Pin:** with the level on the input. |
| Ignition, oil pressure, battery charge, fuel level, air filter | **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**. |
| Marker sensor | Only the common lines. |
| Tramline actuator | **Status:** **Pulled in**, **Pulled out**, **Working** while the shutter moves, or **Unknown**. |
| Dispenser electric motor | **Status:** **Working**, or **Faulty** while any alarm of the motor is active; then **“Last fault:”** with the controller's code, if there has been one ([codes](motor-fault-codes.md)). A universal controller adds **IN1[ ] IN2[ ] IN3[ ]** with the levels on its three inputs. |
| Liquid fertilizer pump controller | **Status:** **Working** or **Faulty**. With a fault, **“Last fault:”** and the code. Without one: **Flow=** in L/min, **Load=** in per cent, and **Pressure sensor: No** if there is none, otherwise **Pressure sensor=** in Bar with the raw signal in mA in brackets. Dashes stand for a value the controller cannot give. |

## The eight states of a seed or fertilizer sensor

| **Status** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Working** | Normal. |
| **Working:Tramline** | Normal; the sensor is in the tramline control mode for the current bout, or its product application is switched off. |
| **Configuring** | The sensor has received new settings and is applying them. |
| **Calibration in progress** | The sensor runs its initial calibration. It takes a few seconds. |
| **Clogged** | The optical channel is blocked — most likely a blocked seed tube. Red. |
| **Light struck** | Too much light falls into the optical channel; the sensor may miscount. Red. |
| **Faulty** | The sensor reports a fault of its own. Red. |
| **Unknown** | Another fault that cannot be identified. Red. |


# Travel speed sensor

Everything the panel counts — area, rates, deviations — is worked out from the distance travelled. **A speed sensor that is out by a tenth makes every other figure on the panel wrong by a tenth.** Set its parameters first, then calibrate it ([Calibrate the speed sensor](calibrate-speed.md)).

Touch and hold the speed field on the home screen to open the context menu of the speed sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). All its parameters need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). The menu also offers **“Speed calibration”** directly, under **“Information”**, while the machine stands still.

![The context menu of the speed sensor at the Agronomist level. A limit that is switched off reads “No”.](figures/five-ctx-speed-sensor)

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses”** | The number of pulses the sensor gives per turn of the wheel. | 1 … 1000; 6 |
| **“Count period”** | The number of pulses the panel averages over before it works out the speed afresh; a sudden change of speed is taken at once. Hidden when the sensor is on an input device. | 1 … 1000; 1 |
| **“Diameter, cm”** | The wheel diameter. | 10 … 200; 60 |
| **“Factor, %”** | A correction of the distance per wheel turn: the panel counts the wheel circumference times this factor. 100 takes the circumference as it is. **The speed calibration rewrites it.** Number pad. | 1 … 10000; 100 |
| **“Seeding criteria”** | **“Yes”** — the section alarms are watched only while the machine moves; **“No”** — also while it stands. Hidden, and always **“Yes”**, in the **“Precise”** mode and on a machine with dispenser motors or a pump. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“Yes”** |
| **“Min speed, km/h”** | Below this speed the home screen shows **“FASTER”**. **“No”** (0) switches the check off. | 0 … 99; **“No”** |
| **“Max speed, km/h”** | Above this speed the home screen shows **“SLOWER”**. **“No”** (0) switches the check off. | 0 … 99; **“No”** |
| **“Imitation, km/h”** | A simulated speed. **“No”** (0) — the real sensor is used. | **0 … 20**; **“No”** |
| **“GPS”** | Take the speed from an external receiver. Shown only when one is in use. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** |
| **“Width, cm”** | The track between the two wheels of a two-sensor installation. Shown only with **“Input device (2)”** in the profile. | 0 … 10000; 280 |
| **“GPS internal”** | Take the speed from the receiver built into the panel. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“No”** |

The minimum must be below the maximum, otherwise the panel raises **“Error in settings of Min/Max”** ([Speed sensor alarms](alarms-speed-sensor.md)). With **“GPS internal”** on, the satellite symbol on the home screen shows the reception, and fewer than four satellites raise **“Poor GPS signal quality”** — see [GPS](gps.md).

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Setting “Imitation, km/h” to anything but zero changes two other things by itself.** The panel switches **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** off — they mean nothing against a simulated speed — and says so in a window. And it **locks the product application**, so that nothing is dosed while the machine stands. The lock is the yellow hand on the home screen; to release it, touch and hold an empty place of the right-hand column ([Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md)).

The imitated speed is also **held inside the range the dosing allows**: a value outside it is pulled back to the nearest limit as you set it. While the speed is imitated, the status screen of the sensor shows **“IMITATION”** in yellow. Working without a speed sensor: [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md).

## The status screen

The status screen shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz (with two sensors **F1=** and **F2=**) and the two limits in force. See [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).


# Calibrate the speed sensor

The calibration measures a known distance and corrects **“Factor, %”** of the speed sensor so that the panel's distance matches it. **Before you start, set “Pulses” and “Diameter, cm”** of the sensor ([Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md)) — the calibration corrects the distance per turn; it cannot invent the pulses.

There are two ways in:

- **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”** → **“Speed calibration”** — at the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md));
- **“Speed calibration”** in the context menu of the speed sensor, while the machine stands still. At the **“Operator”** level the panel first asks for the PIN of the Agronomist level; at the **“Agronomist”** level it asks **“Are you sure?”** — tap **“Yes”**.

::: steps
1. Mark out **100 m** on level ground and put the machine at the start.

2. Tap **“Speed calibration”**, and tap it again; coming from the context menu, answer the PIN or the question first. The panel shows **“Pass 100m and press STOP”** with a single **“STOP”** button.

   ![The speed calibration window.](figures/five-calib-speed)

3. Drive the marked distance and stop at the end.

4. Tap **“STOP”**. The panel shows **“Done”** and closes the window by itself.

   ![The panel confirms the calibration.](figures/five-calib-speed-done)
:::

The distance is fixed at 100 m; the panel does not ask for it. It waits half a second after **“STOP”** before reading the counter and checks the connection once more in that moment — a sensor that drops out on the last metre is reported as a lost connection, not as a bad result.

> **NOTE**
>
> **A tap outside the window ends the calibration without a result.** Keep your hand off the screen while driving, and tap only **“STOP”**.

## When it does not work

| **The panel shows** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“No speed sensor”** | The profile has no speed sensor. The calibration does not start. |
| **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”** | The sensor does not answer. |
| **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** | The sensor is out of control. Take it into control ([Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md)). |
| **“FAILURE! The tractor did not move!”** | The counter did not move: the sensor gave no pulses at all — not an inaccurate reading, none. Check the sensor and its cable. |
| **“Calibration canceled!”** | The window was closed some other way than with **“STOP”**. Nothing has changed. |


# Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors

Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors are the same kind of device and share one parameter set. **Almost everything here is common to the whole group**: change it on one sensor and it changes for all sensors of the group. Only two things are set per sensor — whether it is **under control** (**“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”**) and **“Product application”**. Touch and hold the column of any sensor of the group to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

![The context menu of a seed sensor, top part.](figures/five-ctx-seed)

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Product application”** | **Per sensor.** **“No”** — the row deliberately applies nothing, and the panel watches it as a shut-off tramline row. Not offered when every sensor of the group has its own dispenser motor. | **“No”** / **“Yes”** | Agronomist |
| **“Sensitivity”** | The sensitivity of the optical channel. Shown only for the sensor types that use it. | 1 … 120; 80 | Agronomist |
| **“Fraction”** | The sensor's filter for the size of the product particles. The rate, skip and double alarms tell you in which direction to change it. | 1 … 100; 10 | Operator |
| **“Correction”** | A correction of the detection window of the optical channel. Shown only for the sensor type that uses it. | 100 … 3300, steps of 10; 300 | Operator |
| **“Rate error,%”** | How far the actual rate may stand from the target before an alarm. **“Hybrid”** and **“Precise”** modes only. | 5 … 95, steps of 5; 50 | Agronomist |
| **“Doubles error,%”** | The share of doubles that raises an alarm. **“No”** (0) switches the alarm off. **“Precise” mode only.** | 0 … 95; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Skips error,%”** | The share of skips that raises an alarm. **“No”** (0) switches the alarm off. **“Precise” mode only.** | 0 … 95; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Recalculation,m”** / **“Recalculation,sec”** | The stretch the skips and doubles are counted over — in metres on a machine with a speed sensor, in seconds without one. | 10 … 50; 20 | Operator |
| **“Percent of sowing,%”** | The share of the seed sensors under control that must see seed before the panel decides that seeding has started. Seed sensors only; hidden on a machine with dispenser motors or a pump. | 5 … 80, steps of 5; 20 | Agronomist |
| **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** | How much a section that should be shut off for the tramline may still deliver. | 0 … 50; 20 | Agronomist |
| **“Group start address”** | Fertilizer sensors only. Set at commissioning — see [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | — | Agronomist |

> **TIP**
>
> **“Fraction” is the first setting to look at when the rate alarms do not match reality.** Most rate, skip and double alarms name it, with the direction to change it: [Rate alarms](alarms-rate.md), [Doubles and skips](alarms-seeding-quality.md), [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).

The target rates and the alarm level are not menu items: they are changed while you work, on the home screen — see [Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md). The status screen of these sensors shows one of eight states — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor). If a sensor reports **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”** or **“Broken”**: [Sensor clogged or broken](alarms-sensor-state.md).


# Liquid fertilizer sensors and pump controller

Liquid fertilizer is watched by flow sensors in the sections; on some machines a pump controller also drives the pump to the rate. Touch and hold the liquid diagram, or the pump indicator, to open the context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

## Liquid fertilizer section sensors

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses per liter”** | How many pulses the flow sensor gives per litre. Number pad. Hidden when a pump controller is in the profile. | 1 … 60000; 5000 | Agronomist |
| **“Rate error,%”** | How far the actual rate may stand from the target before an alarm. | 5 … 95, steps of 5; 50 | Agronomist |
| **“Tolerable leak to tramline,%”** | How much a section shut off for the tramline may still deliver. | 0 … 50; 20 | Agronomist |
| **“Group start address”** | See [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | — | Agronomist |

The two target rates of these sensors — one for the **“Flow”** mode, one for the **“By area”** mode — have **no menu item**. They are set on the home screen, like every other target rate ([Change the target rate](set-the-target-rate.md)). The mode itself: [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md#liquid-fertilizer-mode).

## Liquid fertilizer pump controller

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Pulses per liter”** | The pulses of the pump's flow measurement per litre; the panel works out the volume pumped from it. Number pad. | 100 … 10000, steps of 10; 3000 | Agronomist |
| **“Pressure sensor”** | The input of the controller the 4–20 mA pressure sensor of the line is wired to; **“No”** — none. | **“No”**, 1, 2; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Pressure boundary, Bar”** | The pressure the sensor reports at the top of its range (20 mA). Set it from the data sheet of the sensor. | 0.0 … 50.0; 16.0 | Agronomist |
| **“Max pressure, Bar”** | Above it the controller raises **“High pressure”**. 0.0 switches the alarm off. | 0.0 … 50.0; 0.0 | Operator |
| **“Section control D.I.”** | An input of the controller that shuts the pump off: **“Shut off(0)”** when the input reads 0, **“Shut off(1)”** when it reads 1; **“No”** — not used. | **“No”** / **“Shut off(0)”** / **“Shut off(1)”** | Agronomist |
| **“Start delay,mS”** | The shortest time, in milliseconds, between two starts of the pump. | 0 … 500, steps of 5; 30 | Service |
| **“Group start address”** | See [Device configuration](device-configuration.md). | — | Agronomist |

The two pressure values are entered with one decimal place. With a pump controller, the liquid rate is always worked by area.

The status screen of the pump controller shows the flow, the pump load and the line pressure — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds). Alarms: [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md), [Rate alarms](alarms-rate.md).


# Dispenser shaft sensor

The dispenser shaft sensor counts the turns of a dispenser driven from the ground wheel. The panel can watch it two ways: by its **rotation** against the speed sensor, or by the **mass** of product it applies. Touch and hold the metering unit icon on the home screen to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

![The context menu of a dispenser sensor with both controls switched off.](figures/five-ctx-dispenser)

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Period, s”** | How long the shaft may give no pulse before it counts as stopped — and how long after the start of seeding or moving the panel waits before it expects rotation. | 1 … 60; 10 | Operator |
| **“Rotation speed control”** | Watch the shaft rotation against the travel speed. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Wheel, pulses”** | Set by the rotation calibration. Shown with rotation control on. | 1 … 65535; 100 | Agronomist |
| **“Dispenser pulses”** | Set by the rotation calibration. Shown with rotation control on. | 1 … 65535; 100 | Agronomist |
| **“Maximum error, %”** | How far the shaft speed may stand from the speed the travel speed asks for before **“Low speed of rotation”** or **“High speed of rotation”**. Shown with rotation control on. | 1 … 50; 10 | Agronomist |
| **“Weight control”** | Watch the dispenser by the **mass** applied instead of by its rotation. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Type of product”** | Which of the four products this dispenser meters. Shown with weight control on. | **“Product 1”** … **“Product 4”** | Agronomist |
| **“Weight, gr”** / **“Weight, pulses”** | Both set by the calibration by weight. Shown with weight control on. Number pad. | 1 … 65535 each | Agronomist |

**Without a speed sensor in the profile, only “Period, s” is offered** — both kinds of control need the travel speed. With **“Weight control”** switched on, the context menu also holds **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**.

> **TIP**
>
> **Prefer weight control to rotation control.** Rotation control notices that the shaft has stopped, not that the product has. **“Weight control”** watches the kilograms per hectare applied and catches an empty or bridged hopper whose dispenser still turns.

## Calibrations

- **Rotation** — for **“Rotation speed control”**: [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md).
- **Mass** — for **“Weight control”**; repeat it whenever the product changes: [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md).

The status screen shows the shaft pulse frequency **F=** in Hz, to three decimals. Its alarms: [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md), and with weight control [Dosing by weight](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md).


# Calibrate the dispenser rotation

This calibration teaches the panel how many dispenser shaft pulses belong to the wheel pulses, so that it can tell a stopped or slipping shaft from a moving machine. It is the basis of **“Rotation speed control”** of the dispenser sensor ([Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)). It writes **“Wheel, pulses”** and **“Dispenser pulses”**.

**Before you start:** the speed sensor **and** every dispenser taking part must be under control and answering. You need the **“Agronomist”** level ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)). Have everything ready to turn the wheel and the dispenser shafts: **once started, the calibration runs until the panel has its result.**

::: steps
1. Open **“Settings”** → **“Seeding machine parameters”**. Tap **“Dispenser calibration”** and swipe right or left to the number of the dispenser — or to **“ALL”** for all of them at once.

2. Tap **“Dispenser calibration”** again. The panel shows **“Calibration”** and a progress bar.

   ![The progress bar of the dispenser calibration.](figures/five-calib-dispenser-progress)

3. Turn the drive wheel and the dispenser shaft together — by hand, or by moving the machine. The bar fills as the counters rise.

4. Keep turning until the bar reaches 100 %. That happens when the speed sensor **and every** dispenser taking part have each given at least **100 pulses**. The bar follows whichever is furthest behind — a dispenser that does not turn holds it at zero.

5. At 100 % the panel beeps once and shows **“Stop rotation!”**. Stop everything.

6. The panel waits until no counter has changed for **two seconds**, then writes the result and shows **“Done”**.
:::

Let the calibration run to the end. If any sensor taking part is out of control when you start, or stops answering on the way, the calibration ends with **“Sensor not controlled! Calibration canceled!”** or **“Connection lost with the sensor! Calibration canceled!”**, and nothing is written.

> **NOTE**
>
> **The stored numbers are not the ones you watched.** If the counts do not fit the parameter range, the panel halves **both** numbers together, again and again, until they fit. The ratio is kept; only the two stored figures come out smaller than what was counted.


# Calibrate the dispenser by weight

This calibration stores how many grams the dispenser delivers per shaft pulse — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”** of the dispenser sensor. Repeat it whenever the product changes. It is done standing, at the **“Operator”** level; the panel raises itself to **“Agronomist”** for the length of the calibration and puts the level back on exit.

**You need:** a container that holds 2 to 60 kg of the product, and scales.

The item is only there when **“Weight control”** is switched on for this dispenser ([Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md)). Every step is a tap on a button of the screen.

::: steps
1. Touch and hold the metering unit icon on the home screen. Tap **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**, and tap it again. The first screen lists the target rates of the products in use, in kg/ha; the product of this dispenser is marked.

   ![The first screen of the calibration by weight.](figures/five-calib-dispenser-weight)

2. Tap **“Calibrate dispenser N”**. If the dispenser cannot be calibrated, a red line stands there instead with the reason: **“Not controlled”**, **“No connection”** or **“FAILURE”**. **“Exit”** leaves.

3. The second screen gives the preparation. Weigh the empty container and write the weight down.

4. Fill the hopper with the product and place the empty container under the dispenser.

5. Turn the rotor until its cells are filled. **This matters more than it looks:** a rotor with empty cells gives short measure for the first turns, and that error lands in the stored figure.

6. Tap **“Go to calibration”**. **“Cancel”** returns to the first screen instead. The third screen counts **“Impulses”** and turns a rotor icon as they arrive.

7. Empty the container and place it under the dispenser again.

8. Turn the dispenser rotor and fill the container as far as possible — **not less than 2 kg and not more than 60 kg**.

9. Tap **“Complete”**. The button appears only after **more than ten pulses**. **“Cancel”** asks **“Are you sure?”** before throwing the measurement away.

10. Weigh the filled container. The number pad asks to **“Enter the difference of the filled and empty container in grams”**. Type the weight of the product alone — **2000 to 60000 g**; the pad offers 10000 — and tap **“OK”**. The panel stores **“Weight, gr”** and **“Weight, pulses”**.
:::

A weight typed outside 2000 … 60000 g is not refused: the panel takes the nearest limit. Weigh carefully and stay inside the range.

> **NOTE**
>
> **A dispenser alarm during the calibration does not stop it** — only a lost connection does. The measurement is mechanical, and the panel keeps out of the way until the container is weighed. A dispenser that is already in alarm cannot start a calibration.


# Dispenser electric motor

An electric motor drives a dispenser at the speed the panel works out from the target rate and the travel speed. Touch and hold its tile on the Motors screen or on the second home screen to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

![The context menu of a metering motor, top part.](figures/five-ctx-motor)

Which items you see depends on the mode of its group: a motor of a group in the **“Precise”** mode drives a seed disk; in **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”** it meters a product by weight.

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Holes in disk”** | The number of holes in the seed disk. **“Precise” mode only.** | 1 … 200; 27 | Operator |
| **“Numerator”** / **“Denominator”** | Together: the gear ratio between the motor and the dispenser shaft. | 1 … 500 each; 10 / 10 | Agronomist |
| **“Rotation direction”** | The direction the motor turns. | **“Forward”** / **“Backward”**; **“Forward”** | Agronomist |
| **“Start delay,mS”** | The shortest time, in milliseconds, between the starts of two motors, so that they do not all start at once. | 0 … 500, steps of 5; 30 | Service |
| **“Section control D.I.”** | An input of the controller that shuts the section off: **“Shut off(0)”** when the input reads 0, **“Shut off(1)”** when it reads 1. | **“No”** / **“Shut off(0)”** / **“Shut off(1)”**; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Rollback when jammed”** | **“Yes”** — when the rotor jams, the motor turns backwards for a moment instead of only stopping. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Group start address”** | Set at commissioning — see [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md). | — | Agronomist |

In the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes the menu also holds:

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”** | Starts the calibration by weight. Shown only while the machine stands still. [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md) | — | Operator |
| **“Type of product”** | Which of the four products this motor meters. | **“Product 1”** … **“Product 4”** | Agronomist |
| **“Weight, gr”** / **“Rotations”** | Both set by the calibration by weight. Number pad. | 1 … 65535 each; 10000 / 100 | Agronomist |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** / **“Maximum, rpm”** | The shaft speed window the rate control may use, with one decimal place. Number pad. | 0.1 … 500.0 each; 0.1 / 500.0 | Agronomist |
| **“Button input”** | The input of the motor controller used as a calibration button; **“No”** — none. | **“No”**, 1 … 3; **“No”** | Agronomist |
| **“Activation signal”** | Which state of that input counts as pressed. | 0 / 1; 1 | Agronomist |

**“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”** are not a safety limit but the window the rate control works in. The speed window shown on the calibration screen is worked out from them together with the roller figures. **“Button input”** and **“Activation signal”** let one person run the motor from the dispenser during the calibration — see [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

The status screen shows **“Working”** or **“Faulty”** and the last fault code ([Read the fault code of an electric motor](motor-fault-codes.md)). Alarms: [Metering motor alarms](alarms-motor-controller.md), [Dosing by weight](alarms-dosing-by-weight.md). The controller itself is set up in [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md).


# Calibrate a metering motor by weight

This calibration stores how much product one turn of the metering roller delivers — **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** of one motor. Repeat it whenever the product or the roller changes. It is done at the **“Operator”** level, on a motor whose group is in the **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”** mode.

**You need:** the machine standing still, a container that holds 1 to 60 kg of the product, and scales.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The item appears only while the machine is standing still.** In motion the panel removes it from the context menu without a message. And while the calibration is open, **every** electric motor on the machine — seed and fertilizer — is held at zero speed: nothing meters. Leaving the calibration returns them all to automatic rate control.

::: steps
1. Touch and hold the tile of the motor on the Motors screen or the second home screen. Tap **“Dispenser calibration(weight)”**, and tap it again.

2. The first screen shows the target rates and, under **“Product dosage speed limitation:”**, the **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** the current settings allow. If it reads **“Can not provide dosage!”** in red, the roller fitted cannot deliver the rate at any speed — calibration will not repair that; fit another roller. Otherwise tap **“Calibrate electric motor N”**. **“Exit”** leaves.

   ![The first screen of the motor calibration.](figures/five-calib-motor-weight)

3. The second screen prepares the rotor. Weigh the empty container and write the weight down. Fill the hopper and place the empty container under the dispenser.

4. Tap **“Fill the rotor cells”**. The motor turns the driven shaft **two turns** and stops by itself. **“Stop motor”** interrupts it. Repeat until the cells are full.

5. Tap **“Go to calibration”**. The third screen shows **“Rotations”** to one decimal.

6. Empty the container and place it under the dispenser again.

7. Tap **“Calibration”**: the motor runs. Tap **“Stop motor”** to stop it. Run and stop as often as needed — the counter keeps a running total. Fill the container as far as possible, **not less than 1 kg and not more than 60 kg**.

8. Tap **“Complete”**. It appears once more than **one full turn** has been made. **“Cancel”** asks **“Are you sure?”** before throwing the measurement away.

9. Weigh the filled container. The number pad asks for the difference of the filled and empty container in grams — **1000 to 60000 g**; the pad offers 10000. Type it and tap **“OK”**. The panel stores **“Weight, gr”** and **“Rotations”** for this motor.
:::

During the rotor filling the motor runs at the middle of its **“Minimum, rpm”** … **“Maximum, rpm”** window, but not faster than 60 rpm.

## Run the motor from a button at the dispenser

If **“Button input”** of the motor is set to an input (1 … 3) and **“Activation signal”** matches the button ([Dispenser electric motor](dispenser-motor.md)), a button on that input runs the motor on the third screen: **the motor runs while the button is held and stops when it is released.** One person can stand at the dispenser with the container instead of walking to the cab between runs. With such a button set up, the motor runs only while the button is held. The screen gives no hint that a button is set up.

## When the calibration stops by itself

The calibration ends with a failure if the motor stops answering, if the motor raises an alarm, or if **ten seconds pass without pulses from the rotation sensor** — then the panel shows **“No data from rotation sensor”**. A jammed or unplugged rotation sensor ends the run rather than quietly storing zero.


# Fan sensor

The fan sensor watches the speed of the fan of a pneumatic drill or planter. Touch and hold the fan icon on the home screen to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** | Below it the panel raises **“Low speed of rotation”**. | 500 … 9000, steps of 500; 3000 | Operator |
| **“Maximum, rpm”** | Above it the panel raises **“High speed of rotation”**. | 500 … 9000, steps of 500; 5000 | Operator |
| **“Pulses”** | How many pulses one turn of the fan gives. | 1 … 60; 2 | Agronomist |

![The context menu of a fan sensor at the Agronomist level.](figures/five-ctx-fan)

The home screen shows the fan speed in rpm beside the icon; the status screen shows the pulse frequency **F=** in Hz. Alarms: [Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms](alarms-rotation.md).


# Pressure sensor

The pressure sensor measures the positive pressure or the vacuum of the air system. Touch and hold the pressure icon on the home screen to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Filter”** | How strongly the sensor smooths its reading. | 1 … 16; 1 | Agronomist |
| **“Minimum, Pa”** | The lower limit of the allowed band. **“No”** (0) switches the low-pressure check off. | 0 … 10000, steps of 100; **“No”** | Operator |
| **“Maximum, Pa”** | The upper limit of the allowed band. **“No”** (0) switches the high-pressure check off. | 0 … 10000, steps of 100; **“No”** | Operator |

The band is watched only while the machine seeds, or moves with the implement in work. Both limits apply to the size of the pressure or vacuum, whichever it is. The limits are set in pascals; the home screen and the status screen show the pressure **P=** in kilopascals (1 kPa = 1000 Pa).

Alarms: [Air pressure](alarms-pressure.md). Giving a new pressure sensor its address: [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md).


# Marker sensors

The marker sensors tell the panel which marker is down. The profile declares **“No”**, **“One”** or **“Both”** ([The profile](profile.md)). Touch and hold the marker icon on the home screen to open the context menu of a marker sensor ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)).

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Values, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Connected marker”** | Which marker the single sensor watches. Hidden when the profile has both markers. | **“Left”** / **“Right”**; **“Left”** | Agronomist |
| **“Signal "down"”** | Which state of the input means the marker is lowered. | 0 / 1; 0 | Agronomist |

The status screen of a marker sensor shows only the common lines. On a machine that makes tramlines, the change of the marker position ends a bout — see [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md#how-the-bout-changes).

> **NOTE**
>
> **The marker sensors are wired to the tramline actuator controller.** One such controller carries the actuator **and** both marker sensors — see [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md).


# Hopper, work position and engine sensors

These sensors report one of two states and nothing more. Touch and hold the icon of any of them on the home screen to open its context menu ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)). Their status screen shows **Pin:** and the level on the input, **"0"** or **"1"**.

## Hopper sensor

The hopper sensor has **no parameters of its own** — its context menu holds only the common items.

Alarm: [Hopper empty](alarms-hopper.md).

## Work position sensor

The work position sensor tells the panel whether the implement is lowered for work or raised for transport. The status screen shows **“Position: Working”** or **“Position: Transporting”**.

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Values, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Transporting position signal”** | Which state of the input means the transport position. | 0 / 1; 0 | Agronomist |
| **“Alarms criteria”** | **“Yes”** — while the implement is raised, the section alarms are not watched. **“No”** — the position does not affect the alarms. Hidden, and always **“Yes”**, on a machine with dispenser motors or a pump. | **“No”** / **“Yes”**; **“Yes”** | Agronomist |

On a machine without markers that makes tramlines, raising the implement ends a bout — see [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md#how-the-bout-changes).

## Engine sensors

**“No battery charge”**, **“Emergency oil pressure”**, **“Ignition”**, **“Low fuel”** and **“Air filter”** are five separate inputs, each switched on in the profile on its own ([The profile](profile.md)).

![The context menu of the oil pressure sensor.](figures/five-ctx-oil-pressure)

| **Parameter** | **What it does** | **Range, default** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Activation signal”** | Which state of the input is the one worth reporting. | 0 / 1; 1 | Agronomist |
| **“Signal delay, sec”** | How long that state must hold before it counts. | 1 … 30; **15 s** for the fuel level, **5 s** for the air filter, **1 s** for the others | Agronomist |

Oil pressure and battery charge are watched only while the ignition is on; fuel level and air filter always. Alarms: [Tractor engine alarms](alarms-tractor.md).


# Tramline actuator

The tramline actuator shuts the sections of the tramline bout. It has two parameters of its own, in its context menu — touch and hold its tile on the Motors screen ([Sensor settings](sensor-settings.md)):

| **Parameter** | **Values** | **Level** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Cutoff position”** | **“Pulled out”** / **“Pulled in”** — the position of the actuator in which its sections are shut off. Default **“Pulled out”**. | Agronomist |
| **“Switch”** | **“when seeding”** / **“always”** — when the actuator is switched. Default **“when seeding”**. | Agronomist |

The rest of its settings live elsewhere:

| **What** | **Where** |
| --- | --- |
| The address and the marker channels of its controller | [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md) |
| The rhythm — which bout shuts which actuator | [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md) |
| Which sections belong to the actuator | **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** — [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md#relation-of-sensors-to-actuators) |

The status screen of the actuator shows **Status:** **Pulled in**, **Pulled out**, **Working** while the shutter is moving, or **Unknown**. Alarms: [Tramline alarms](alarms-tramline.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> **One actuator controller carries three things:** the actuator itself and **both** marker sensors of the bout. That is why a machine with markers and a tramline needs only one such controller.


# Device configuration — before you start

When a system is commissioned, or a sensor is replaced, each new device must be given its address — the number by which the panel finds it on the sensor network. That is done in **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”**, one device at a time.

> **WARNING**
>
> **For authorised service engineers.** A device given the wrong address disappears from the panel or takes the place of another one. Follow these topics or the instructions of an Agriwelt GmbH engineer, and do not try menu items at random.

## Prepare

::: steps
1. **Disconnect every sensor** from the network connector of the panel.

2. **Connect only the one device** that is to be given a new address.

3. Switch the panel on. Alarms about lost communication appear — close them all with **“Close”** ([How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md)).

4. Raise the access level to **“Agronomist”** — see [Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md).

5. Tap the home screen with two fingers, then tap **“Service”** twice and **“Sensors Configuration”** twice. The menu offers four kinds of device: **“Seed sensor”**, **“Pressure sensor”**, **“Concentrator-8”** and **“Tramline actuator”**.

   ![The Sensors Configuration menu.](figures/five-menu-sensorcfg)
:::

## The pattern

All four menus work the same way:

| **Item** | **What it is** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Sensor address”** / **“Device address”** | Which device the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”** and the panel talks to the single device that answers. Tapping the selected item again starts a **search**; each further tap steps to the next device found. |
| **“New address”** | The address the device is to take. Set it with a swipe right or left. |
| **“Set”** | Writes it. Tap it, and tap it again. **“Done”** means the device has accepted it. |

**What “Set” can answer:**

| **Message** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Done”** | The device has taken the new address. |
| **“More than one device in network!”** | With **“AUTO”**, more than one device answers. Disconnect all but one. |
| **“No connection”** | No device answers. Check the cable and the power of the device. |
| **“Address: … is used!”** | The address you chose belongs to another device already. Choose another. |

> **CAUTION**
>
> **The search on the address item is not a harmless look.** It talks to the devices on the network. Use it only with a single device on the cable, never on an assembled machine. With an address typed by hand instead of **“AUTO”**, the panel writes to whatever answers on that address.

**Afterwards, every time:** disconnect the device and connect it again, return to the home screen and check that it appears where it should. Then set the level back to **“Operator”** — or switch the panel off and on, which does the same.

## The devices

| **Device** | **Topic** |
| --- | --- |
| Seed sensor | [Configure a seed sensor](configure-seed-sensor.md) |
| Pressure sensor | [Configure a pressure sensor](configure-pressure-sensor.md) |
| HUB8 input device — **“Concentrator-8”** on the screen | [Configure a HUB8](configure-hub8.md) |
| Tramline actuator controller | [Configure a tramline actuator controller](configure-tramline-actuator.md) |
| Electric motor controllers — their own way in | [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md) |


# Configure a seed sensor

For a seed sensor the new address is simply **the number of the row** — the same number the operator sees under the column on the home screen. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

::: steps
1. Open **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Seed sensor”** — tap each item twice. The menu has three items: **“Sensor address”**, **“New address”** and **“Set”**.

   ![The Seed sensor configuration menu.](figures/five-cfg-seed)

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Tap **“New address”** and swipe right or left to the row number.

4. Tap **“Set”**, and tap it again. The panel answers **“Done”** and, below it, **“Found #”** with the number the sensor had until now.

   ![The panel confirms with “Done”. The number after “Found #” is left out of the picture.](figures/five-info-done)

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. On the home screen, check that it appears under its row.
:::

If the panel answers **“More than one device in network!”**, another device is still on the cable. If it answers **“No connection”**, the sensor does not answer — check its cable and power.

When all sensors are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on. The parameters of the seed sensors: [Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).


# Configure a pressure sensor

Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this sensor on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level. The menu has the same three items as every configuration menu. The address values are not printed in this manual: **take them from the data sheet of the system.**

::: steps
1. Open **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Pressure sensor”** — tap each item twice. The menu shows **“Sensor address”**, **“New address”** and **“Set”**.

2. Leave **“Sensor address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Tap **“New address”**. The panel proposes the value for the first pressure sensor by itself; each further sensor takes the next one. Check the value against the data sheet and correct it with a swipe right or left if needed.

4. Tap **“Set”**, and tap it again. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the sensor and connect it again. On the home screen, check that its indicator appears.
:::

When all sensors are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on. Its parameters: [Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md).


# Configure a HUB8

The HUB8 carries several devices at once. On the panel it is called **“Concentrator-8”**. Its menu is longer than the others: after the device address come its **eight channels**, each with a type and a number. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this HUB8 on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

| **Item** | **What it is** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Device address”** | Which HUB8 the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”**. |
| **“Channel 1 type”** … **“Channel 8 type”** | What is wired to the channel: **“Seed sensors”** or **“Input device”**. |
| **“Channel 1 address”** … **“Channel 8 address”** | Which device of that kind it is: for a seed sensor, the number of its row; for an input device, the value from the data sheet of the system. |
| **“Set”** | Writes all channels to the HUB8. |

![The Concentrator-8 menu with its first channels.](figures/five-cfg-hub8)

The type and the number together make the device appear on the home screen in the right place.

::: steps
1. Open **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Concentrator-8”** — tap each item twice.

2. Leave **“Device address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. For each channel that carries a device, tap its type item — **“Channel 1 type”** for channel 1 — and swipe to the type, then tap its address item — **“Channel 1 address”** — and swipe to the number. Leave a channel that carries nothing as it is.

4. Swipe up to **“Set”** at the end of the menu, tap it, and tap it again. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the HUB8 and connect it again. On the home screen, check that each device appears in its place.
:::

Two channels of the same type cannot have the same number: **“Set”** then refuses with **“Invalid profile!”** and writes nothing.

When all devices are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on.


# Configure a tramline actuator controller

The actuator controller carries three things at once — the tramline actuator and the two marker sensors of the bout — and each has its own line. That is why one controller serves an actuator and both markers. Prepare first as in [Device configuration](device-configuration.md): only this controller on the cable, **“Agronomist”** level.

| **Item** | **What it is** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Device address”** | Which controller the menu talks to. Leave it at **“AUTO”**. |
| **“Actuator”** | The number of the tramline actuator this controller drives, or **“No”** if it drives none. |
| **“Input device, channel 1”** | The first marker sensor, or **“No”**. |
| **“Input device, channel 2”** | The second marker sensor, or **“No”**. |
| **“Set”** | Writes the three lines to the controller. |

![The configuration menu of a tramline actuator controller, all lines still at “No”.](figures/five-cfg-actuator)

::: steps
1. Open **“Service”** → **“Sensors Configuration”** → **“Tramline actuator”** — tap each item twice.

2. Leave **“Device address”** at **“AUTO”**.

3. Set **“Actuator”**, **“Input device, channel 1”** and **“Input device, channel 2”**: tap each line and swipe right or left to its value.

4. Tap **“Set”**, and tap it again. The panel answers **“Done”**.

5. Disconnect the controller and connect it again. On the home screen, check that the actuator and the markers appear.
:::

**“Set”** refuses with **“Invalid profile!”**, and writes nothing, when all three lines are at **“No”**, or when both marker channels carry the same number.

When all devices are done, set the level back to **“Operator”**, or switch the panel off and on. The actuator's own settings: [Tramline actuator](tramline-actuator.md); the markers: [Marker sensors](marker-sensors.md).


# Configure the motor controllers

The controllers that drive the metering motors are not addressed from **“Sensors Configuration”**. They have their own way in, their own choice of controller kind and their own parameters.

> **WARNING**
>
> **For authorised service engineers.** As with every device on the cable: **one controller connected at a time.** The panel writes to whichever controller answers.

## Open the motor controller menu

::: steps
1. Raise the level to **“Agronomist”** ([Enable the Agronomist level](enable-agronomist-level.md)).

2. Tap the home screen with two fingers, tap **“Service”** twice, then **“Electric motors”** twice. The diagnostic screen of the controllers opens on motor 1. The same screen opens from **“Electric motors”** in the context menu of a motor.

   ![The Electric motors screen of motor 1, page “Registers”.](figures/five-motors-registers)

3. Tap the screen with **two fingers**. Two items appear: **“Change address”** and **“Configuration”**.

   ![The menu of the Electric motors screen.](figures/five-motors-menu)
:::

## Change the address

::: steps
1. Tap **“Change address”**, and tap it again. Three items open.

2. **“Motor address”** — the address the controller answers on now. Leave it as found.

3. **“New address”** — the address it is to take. **Take it from the data sheet of the system; the values are not printed in this manual.**

4. Tap **“Set”**, and tap it again, to write it.
:::

## Choose the controller kind

**“Configuration”** opens the choice of controller kind, offered by number. The panel reads the kind back from the controller and opens on the one that answers. Choosing another kind by hand is how a replacement board is set up — not a way to change what a motor is.

| **Kind** | **What it is** |
| --- | --- |
| **“1)universal”** | The universal controller: two DC channels or one stepper channel on the same board. |
| **“2)DC motor”** | A DC motor controller. |
| **“3)STEPPER fw0.006+”** | A stepper controller, firmware 0.006 and later. |
| **“4)BGxxCI”** | A BG45CI motor with the controller built in, on the older board. |

If the controller that answers does not suit the menu, the panel says so: **“Wrong controller type!”**, **“Old firmware version!”** or **“Wrong controller work mode!”**.

## Set the parameters

Every configuration menu ends with **“Set”**, and **“Set”** carries a value of its own — the **address group**: **“Motor address”** (this controller only), **“ALL”**, **“All-Seeding”** or **“All-Fertilizer”**. **Nothing reaches the controller until “Set” is entered** — the items above it change the numbers the panel holds, not those the controller runs on. **“Set”** answers **“Done”**, **“FAILURE”** or **“No connection”**; a group that has no motors in the profile is answered with **“EM of dispensers is missing in profile”**.

| **Kind** | **What it is given** |
| --- | --- |
| STEPPER | **“Pulses”** 1 … 8192 — the pulses of one turn of the motor shaft; **“Motor type”** from a list; **“Set”**. |
| BGxxCI | **“Pulses”** 1 … 8192; **“Set”**. Nothing else — the controller carries the rest. |
| DC motor | **“Pulses”**, **“Motor type”**, the regulator terms **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”** (0 … 65535, read as hundredths), **“TURBINA”** 0/1, and two speed–time pairs **“TIME1”** / **“SPEED1”**, **“TIME2”** / **“SPEED2”**; **“Set”**. |
| universal | The largest set, in three menus: **“Work mode”**, **“Inputs setup”** and **“Parameters”**. |

The **“Parameters”** menu of the universal controller:

| **Parameter** | **Range** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Motor type”** | 0 … 255, from the controller's own table |
| **“Pulses”** | 1 … 8192 per shaft turn |
| **“Acceleration,Ms”** / **“Deceleration,Ms”** | 50 … 65535 — the ramp up and down |
| **“Minimum, rpm”** / **“Maximum, rpm”** | 0 … 65535 — the shaft speed window |
| **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”** | 0 … 65535, hundredths |
| **“!! Temp,\*C”** | 0 … 200 — the temperature at which the controller alarms |
| **“I_peak,A”** / **“I_peak,mS”** | the peak current, in tenths of an ampere, and how long it may be drawn |
| **“I_push,A”** / **“I_push,Sec”** | the breakaway current and its time |
| **“I_hilo,A”** / **“I_hilo,Sec”** | the sustained-current threshold and its time |
| **“Set”** | writes all of it, at the chosen address group |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The current and temperature limits protect the motor.** They are the controller's own protection thresholds: set them from the data sheet of the motor, not by trying values until the alarms stop.
