The four kind names and the items **“PID kP”**, **“PID kI”**, **“PID kD”**, **“TURBINA”**, **“TIME1”**, **“SPEED1”**, **“TIME2”**, **“SPEED2”**, **“!! Temp,\*C”**, **“I_peak,A”**, **“I_push,A”**, **“I_hilo,A”** and their time partners read the same in every language of the panel.

Reading what the controller reports: [Motor controller diagnostics](motor-controller-diagnostics.md).


# Motor controller diagnostics

The **Electric motors** screen shows, live, what a motor controller reports about itself. Open it with a two-finger tap on the home screen → **“Service”** → **“Electric motors”**, or with **“Electric motors”** in the context menu of a motor — both at the **“Agronomist”** level. The working view of the motors is a different screen: [Motors screen](motors-screen.md).

::: {.anatomy fig="five-motors-registers"}
1. **“Mode”** — tap it to switch the page: **“Registers”**, then **“Statistics”**.
2. **“Motor #”** with a number — which controller is shown (the number is left out of the picture). Swipe **right** for the next number, **left** for the previous one.
3. **“Registers”** — the name of the page. A universal controller has two register pages, **“Registers-1”** and **“Registers-2”**.
4. **The status word** — sixteen bits of the controller; a lit (yellow) cell is a bit that is set.
5. **The legend of the bits** — the number and the name of each bit. [Table below](#the-status-bits).
6. **“Speed”** / **“Target speed”** — what the shaft is doing against what the panel asked for. A gap that does not close is the first sign of a load the motor cannot carry.
7. **“Error code”** / **“Act.posit.”** — the controller's own error number ([codes](motor-fault-codes.md)), and the position it counts itself at.
8. **“Volt.mot.,mV”** / **“Volt.elec.,mV”** — the voltage at the motor and at the electronics, in millivolts. A motor voltage far below the electronics voltage means the supply sags under load.
9. **“Temperat.,C”** / **“Current,mA”** — the controller's temperature and the current it draws. Compare the current with **“I_hilo,A”** set for this motor ([Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md)).

The **“Registers”** page of a motor, standing.
:::

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Tap **“Mode”** | Next page. |
| Swipe right / left | Next / previous controller number. The numbers run from 1 to 127 and go round; a number without a controller shows nothing useful. |
| Two-finger tap | The menu: **“Change address”**, **“Configuration”** — see [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md). |
| Three-finger tap, or long swipe up | Close the screen. |

## The status bits

| **Bit** | **Name** | **Bit** | **Name** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Enable | 8 | Toggle |
| 1 | Error | 9 | CmdTgl |
| 2 | Warn. | 10 | CmdErr |
| 3 | Moving | 11 | StpHalt |
| 4 | Reach | 12 | LimCur |
| 5 | Limit | 13 | LimVel |
| 6 | FolErr | 14 | LimPos |
| 7 | HomDone | 15 | LimSVel |

The legend is drawn in English on every panel, whatever its language: it is a bit map of the controller, not a message to the operator.

## The fault counters

![The Statistics page of a motor.](figures/five-motors-statistics)

The **“Statistics”** page shows the faults this motor has collected **on the active field** — they are part of the field statistics, not of the motor:

| **Counter** | **What it counts** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Jammed”** | The rotor stalled and the controller had to give up or back off. |
| **“Disconnects”** | The controller stopped answering. |
| **“Other”** | Everything else the controller reported. |
| **“In failure”** | The distance in metres this motor spent in a fault state. |

Each counter is **white at zero and red once it is not**. A red figure does not mean the motor is faulty now — it means it was, somewhere on this field, and the seed placed there is worth a look. To read another field, make it the active field first ([Statistics screen](statistics-screen.md)).


# The Service menu

Tap the home screen with two fingers, then tap **“Service”** twice. The menu itself is shown from the **“Agronomist”** level up; which items you see depends on the level ([Access levels](access-levels.md)).

![The Service menu at the Service level.](figures/five-menu-service)

| **Item** | **Level** | **What it is** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Profile”** | Agronomist | Which devices the machine has, and how many. [The profile](profile.md) |
| **“Sensors Configuration”** | Agronomist | Giving devices their address. [Device configuration](device-configuration.md) |
| **“Registers”** | Agronomist | A raw register view. Not part of any procedure. |
| **“Electric motors”** | Agronomist | The diagnostic screen and the configuration of the metering motor controllers. [Configure the motor controllers](configure-motor-controllers.md) |
| **“Serial number”** | Service | The serial number of the panel, entered once at manufacture. |
| **“Imitation mode”** | Service | **“No”** / **“Yes”** — the panel works from simulated data. See the warning below. |
| **“Count seeds always”** | Agronomist | **“No”** / **“Yes”** — **“Yes”** shows the seed counters in the **“Flow”** and **“Hybrid”** modes too; otherwise they are shown in the **“Precise”** mode only. |
| **“Enter key”** | Agronomist | Enters the licence key that takes the panel out of the demonstration state. Shown only while the panel is in that state. |
| **“Set trial”** | Service | Starts the demonstration period. |
| **“Trial, hours”** | Service | 1 … 999 — how long that period lasts. |

Four further items — the tracker protocol, two switches for logging to the memory card and the display type — exist in the firmware but are set never to be shown. They cannot be reached at any level.

> **WARNING**
>
> **“Imitation mode” is not a test aid to be left on.** With it on, the panel works from figures it makes up: every number on every screen and every entry in the statistics is invented. The clock slot of the home screen shows **IMITAT** in yellow while it is on. Switch it off before the machine goes to work — and check it if a panel reports a plausible field it never sowed.

**“Imitation mode”** is shown in English whatever language the panel is set to.


# How alarms work

An alarm is a window that opens over the working screen, with the alarm sound. It tells you that one device — a sensor, an actuator, a motor controller — or the system as a whole has found a fault. The alarm topics in this section are grouped by the device that raises the alarm. **Look for the words you see on the screen**, not for a description of them.

## When the panel raises an alarm

A fault is not reported the moment it appears. **The condition must hold without a break for the time set in “Alarm delay” before the alarm window opens.**

| **Setting** | **Value** |
| --- | --- |
| Where it is set | **“Settings”** menu, item **“Alarm delay”**, at the **“Operator”** level. See [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md). |
| Range | **2 to 20 seconds**, in steps of 1 second. |
| Default | **3 seconds.** A value outside the range is reset to the default by itself. |

A short delay makes the panel react quickly, but also to brief disturbances — a single bump, a momentary gap in the seed flow. A long delay keeps the screen quiet, but a real fault can run for up to twenty seconds before you are told.

> **TIP**
>
> **If the system alarms too often on a rough field, raise “Alarm delay” first.** Change the sensor settings only when a longer delay does not help.

Two cases do not follow the delay:

- **Lost communication** is counted in polls, not in seconds. **“Connection lost”** appears after **three polls in a row** without an answer from the device.
- **Right after a sensor has been set up**, its alarms are not processed for a short blocking period. This prevents a burst of alarms while a device is being configured.

## The alarm window

::: {.anatomy fig="five-alarm-window"}
1. **“FAILURE!”** — the title of every alarm window, on a red bar, whatever the fault. It is not the fault itself.
2. **The alarm text** — the fault. Look it up under this text in the alarm topics.
3. **The kind of device** that raises the alarm — here a hopper sensor. The same text can come from different devices; this line tells you which.
4. **The number of the device** — here hopper 2. When several devices of the same kind raise the same alarm, they share one window and are listed together, for example **#3-5,8**.
5. **“Close”** — closes this alarm. [Below](#closing-an-alarm).

The alarm window of an empty hopper.
:::

An over-current alarm of a motor adds a line with the current the controller measured, in amperes. The alarms of the panel itself — for example **“User is Agronomist!”** — have no device line; their text starts with the line **“HOME - close message”**. They are closed like every other alarm, with **“Close”**.

## Closing an alarm

**Tap “Close” in the window.** This alarm closes and the sound stops. If more alarms are waiting, the next one opens. **Nothing else closes an alarm window** — taps elsewhere, swipes and the three-finger tap are ignored while it is open.

Closing a window does not repair the fault. The alarms of a device that are still active are counted on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).

## Alarms are hidden at the higher access levels

At the **“Agronomist”** and **“Service”** levels no alarm windows are shown — apart from the one warning that says so, [User is Agronomist](alarms-access-level.md) — and the faults without a window stay silent too. The alarms are not lost: they wait. When you return to **“Operator”**, the panel drops the ones that have gone away and shows the ones that are still true, one after another. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).

## Alarms without a window

Two faults are not shown as a window, because you have to see the working screen while you correct them. At the **“Operator”** level the alarm sound plays while they last, as long as no alarm window is open:

- **“SLOWER”** or **“FASTER”** — the travel speed is outside the limits set for the speed sensor. The speed field shows the word. See [Indicators](indicators.md#speed).
- **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** — rows run under the control line of their diagram. See [The section diagram](section-diagram.md#the-line-rows-under-it-are-not-under-control).

## How the alarm topics are written

Every alarm has its own heading with the text exactly as on the screen; where the message has two lines on the panel, both lines are given. Under it: what the panel has detected, and what to check, in the order a mechanic checks it — the quick checks on the panel first, then the machine, then the device itself.

> **NOTE**
>
> If the checks do not clear the fault, call the service support.


# Any device: connection lost or wrong device type

These two alarms are not tied to one kind of device. The name of the device in the alarm window tells you which one is affected. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Connection lost”

**What it means.** The panel has received no answer from the device in three polls in a row. This applies to sensors, actuators, controllers and input devices alike.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The device is connected to the network.
2. The cable and the connector of the device.
3. The power supply of the device. It must meet the values in the device passport.
4. The device is meant to be there: a device in the [profile](profile.md) that is not fitted raises this alarm too. Leave such a device out of control ([Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md)).

## “Wrong device type!”

**What it means.** A device of another kind answers where the panel expects a device of this kind. The cause is either a wrong setting in the system profile or a wrong configuration of the device itself.

**What to do:** call the service support. Do not try to correct it by changing the profile or the device configuration at random — see [Device configuration](device-configuration.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The status screen of a device shows the same two states as **“No connection”** and **“Wrong device type!”** in red — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md).


# Fan or dispenser shaft: speed alarms

The fan sensor and the dispenser shaft sensor use the same two messages. **The device name in the alarm window tells you which one it is.** How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Low speed of rotation” / “High speed of rotation”

**What it means.** The fan or the dispenser shaft turns slower or faster than allowed. For the fan the limits are **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”**; for the dispenser shaft the panel compares it with the speed the travel speed asks for, within **“Maximum error, %”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The component being watched — the fan or the dispenser and its drive.
2. The settings of the sensor: for the fan **“Minimum, rpm”**, **“Maximum, rpm”** and **“Pulses”** — see [Fan sensor](fan-sensor.md); for the dispenser — see [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. **Dispenser only:** the travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
4. The sensor itself is serviceable.
5. **Dispenser only:** run the calibration — see [Calibrate the dispenser rotation](calibrate-dispenser-rotation.md).

## “No rotation”

**What it means.** The dispenser shaft does not turn while the machine seeds or moves. Only the dispenser shaft sensor raises this alarm. The shaft counts as stopped when no pulse has come for **“Period, s”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The dispenser and its drive.
2. The settings of the sensor, above all **“Period, s”** — see [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. The sensor itself is serviceable.


# Hopper empty

The hopper sensor sits in the hopper at a fixed height. It reports when the product falls below it. On the home screen the hopper icon turns from full green to empty red. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Hopper empty”

**What it means.** The level of the product in the hopper is very low. The hopper needs refilling.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Fill the hopper.
2. If the product stands above the height at which the sensor is mounted and the alarm stays, check that the sensor is serviceable. Its status screen shows the level on its input as **"0"** or **"1"** — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).

The hopper sensor has no settings of its own beyond the common ones — see [Hopper, work position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md).


# Air pressure too high or too low

The pressure sensor measures the positive pressure or the vacuum of the air system. Both alarms look at the size of the pressure or vacuum, whichever it is, and only while the machine seeds or moves with the implement in work. The limits are described in [Pressure sensor](pressure-sensor.md). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure or vacuum is greater than **“Maximum, Pa”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Reduce the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The position of the regulating damper of the air intake, if there is one.
3. The tube to the pressure sensor is connected correctly, and the measuring line is free of blockages.

## “Low pressure”

**What it means.** The measured pressure or vacuum is less than **“Minimum, Pa”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. Increase the speed of the fan or turbine.
2. The position of the regulating damper of the air intake, if there is one.
3. The air duct for leaks.
4. The tube to the pressure sensor is connected correctly, and the measuring line is free of blockages.

> **NOTE**
>
> The liquid fertilizer pump controller has its own **“High pressure”** alarm for the liquid line. It is a different alarm — see [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md).


# Application rate too low or too high

The section sensors — seed, dry fertilizer and liquid fertilizer — compare the rate they measure with the target. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

| **Mode of the group** | **“Under allowable rate”** | **“Over allowable rate”** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Flow”** | The flow falls below the alarm level — the control line of the diagram. | Not raised. |
| **“Hybrid”**, **“Precise”** | The rate falls below the target by more than **“Rate error,%”**. | The rate rises above the target by more than **“Rate error,%”**. |

> **TIP**
>
> **Check the travel speed first.** Every rate per metre or per hectare is worked out from the distance travelled. If the speed on the screen is wrong, every rate is wrong by the same amount, and the sensors are not to blame.

## “Under allowable rate”

**What it means.** A section sensor — seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer — has measured too little product during work.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. There is enough product in the hoppers or in the tank.
2. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
3. Seed or dry fertilizer sensor: **“Fraction”**. The value may have to be **reduced**. See [Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
4. Liquid fertilizer sensor: **“Pulses per liter”**. The value may have to be **reduced**. See [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).
5. Seed sensor: its status on the status screen (**“Information”** in its context menu) — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).
6. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “Over allowable rate”

**What it means.** A section sensor — seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer — has measured too much product during work.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. Seed or dry fertilizer sensor: **“Fraction”**. The value may have to be **increased**.
3. Liquid fertilizer sensor: **“Pulses per liter”**. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. Seed sensor: its status on the status screen.
5. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “NOT UNDER CONTROL” — no window

When rows run under the control line, the home screen shows **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** in red and, at the **“Operator”** level, the alarm sound plays — but no alarm window opens. The rows under the line are not guarded.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. The alarm level of the diagram: is it above the rate the machine really applies? Lower it, or let the panel set it — [Set the alarm level](set-the-alarm-level.md).
3. There is enough product in the hoppers or in the tank.
4. **“Fraction”** of the seed or fertilizer sensors, or **“Pulses per liter”** of the liquid sensors — the value may have to be **reduced**.
5. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

What the line means: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md#the-line-rows-under-it-are-not-under-control).


# Too many doubles or skips

Doubles and skips are counted only in the **“Precise”** mode of seeding — on a precision planter. Each alarm is raised only if its limit is set: **“Doubles error,%”** and **“Skips error,%”** at **“No”** switch it off. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High % of doubles”

**What it means.** The share of doubles the sensor counts is higher than **“Doubles error,%”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. **“Doubles error,%”** in the settings of the seed sensors — is the limit sensible? See [Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
3. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the seed sensors. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. The sensor's status on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).
5. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

## “High % of skips”

**What it means.** The share of skips the sensor counts is higher than **“Skips error,%”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed.
2. There is enough seed in the hoppers.
3. **“Skips error,%”** in the settings of the seed sensors — is the limit sensible?
4. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the seed sensors. The value may have to be **reduced**.
5. The sensor's status on its status screen.
6. The metering unit: is it serviceable, and is it adjusted correctly?

The stretch over which the shares are counted is **“Recalculation,m”** of the seed sensors. How the skips and doubles look on the diagram: [The section diagram](section-diagram.md).


# Tramline: actuator stalled or product in the tramline

The tramline actuator shuts the sections of the tramline bout. Two gate position sensors tell the panel where its shutter stands. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Stall”

**What it means.** The tramline actuator has jammed.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The gate position sensors of the actuator are serviceable.
2. The mechanism of the tramline actuator is serviceable.

## “Illegal state”

**What it means.** The actuator reports a position that cannot be: both gate position sensors have triggered at the same time. With a serviceable installation this cannot happen.

**What to check:** the gate position sensors are serviceable.

## “Seeding to tramline”

**What it means.** A section that should be shut off for the tramline still delivers too much product. The seed sensor, the dry fertilizer sensor or the liquid fertilizer sensor of that section has measured it in the tramline control mode.

**Seed sensor or dry fertilizer sensor — check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit and the flow cut-off mechanism are serviceable.
2. **“Toler.sowing to tramline,%”** in the settings of the group of section sensors. The value may have to be **increased**. See [Seed sensors and dry fertilizer sensors](seed-and-fertilizer-sensors.md).
3. **“Fraction”** in the settings of the group of the alarming sensor. The value may have to be **increased**.
4. The sensor's status on its status screen — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).

**Liquid fertilizer sensor — check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit and the flow cut-off mechanism are serviceable.
2. **“Tolerable leak to tramline,%”** in the settings of the group of section sensors. The value may have to be **increased**. See [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).

A sensor whose **“Product application”** is set to **“No”** is watched the same way — as a shut-off row.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> Which sections belong to which actuator is set in **“Relation of sensors to actuators”** — [Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md#relation-of-sensors-to-actuators). The rhythm: [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md).


# Seed or fertilizer sensor clogged, light-struck or broken

The seed and dry fertilizer sensors count the product optically: an emitter shines across the channel, a receiver sees each grain. These alarms report the state of the sensor itself, not the rate. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Clogged”

**What it means.** The seed or dry fertilizer sensor has detected that its optical channel is blocked.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Remove the blockage.
2. Check for a build-up of dust in the channel.
3. Check the power supply of the sensor. It must meet the values in the device passport.

## “Light struck”

**What it means.** The seed or fertilizer sensor has detected an extremely high level of light in its optical channel.

**What to do:** keep direct sunlight out of the optical channel of the sensor.

## “Broken”

**What it means.** The seed or dry fertilizer sensor has detected a fault of its own. It may have to be replaced. Its status screen shows **“Faulty”**.

**What to do:** check the power supply of the sensor. It must meet the values in the device passport. If the power supply is in order, the sensor may have to be replaced — call the service support.

## “Old firmware! Wrong S&D calc!”

**What it means.** A **dry fertilizer** sensor with outdated firmware is in use while the fertilizers are in the **“Precise”** mode. It counts, but its skips and doubles cannot be trusted.

**What to do:** call the service support to have the firmware of the sensor updated — or set **“Mode of fertilizers”** to **“Flow”** or **“Hybrid”** ([Seeding machine parameters](seeding-machine-parameters.md)).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The status screen of the sensor shows the same states — **“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”**, **“Faulty”** — in red: [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#the-eight-states-of-a-seed-or-fertilizer-sensor).


# Engine: oil pressure, battery charge, fuel, air filter

All engine sensors share one alarm text: **“FAILURE”**. **The name of the sensor under the text tells you which one has triggered.** Oil pressure and battery charge are watched only while the ignition is on; fuel level and air filter always. How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md). The settings named below are described in [Hopper, work position and engine sensors](hopper-position-engine-sensors.md).

## “FAILURE” — “Emergency oil pressure”

**What it means.** The low oil pressure sensor has triggered.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The low oil pressure sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the low oil pressure sensor.
3. If an ignition sensor is in the profile: is its control switched on?
4. If an ignition sensor is in the profile: is it serviceable?

## “FAILURE” — “No battery charge”

**What it means.** The battery is not being charged.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The battery charge sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the battery charge sensor.
3. If an ignition sensor is in the profile: is its control switched on?
4. If an ignition sensor is in the profile: is it serviceable?

## “FAILURE” — “Low fuel”

**What it means.** Little fuel is left in the tank.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The fuel level sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the fuel level sensor.
3. **“Signal delay, sec”** in the settings of the fuel level sensor. The default is **15 seconds**.

## “FAILURE” — “Air filter”

**What it means.** The air filter is clogged.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The air filter sensor is serviceable.
2. **“Activation signal”** in the settings of the air filter sensor.
3. **“Signal delay, sec”** in the settings of the air filter sensor. The default is **5 seconds**.

The ignition sensor itself never raises an alarm window: a yellow key on the home screen only says the ignition is off ([Indicators](indicators.md#engine-sensors)).


# Product rate by weight too low, too high, or impossible

These alarms are raised by the system as a whole, not by one device. They exist **for each of the four products** separately: the number in the message is the number of the product. How far a product may stand from its target is **“Product rate error,%”** in the **“Settings”** menu ([The Settings menu](settings-menu.md)). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Rate of Product 1” / “is to low!” — or — “is to high!”

The same for Product 2, 3 and 4. The panel writes the message in this spelling.

**What it means.** The product is applied below or above its target rate in kilograms per hectare by more than **“Product rate error,%”**.

**Product metered by an electric motor — check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product.
2. The speed limits in force, on the status screen of the speed sensor — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).
3. The settings of the electric motor that drives the dispenser shaft — see [Dispenser electric motor](dispenser-motor.md).
4. The metering unit.
5. The rotation sensor of the electric motor is serviceable.
6. The working load of the motor. **Below 20 % or above 80 %**, try a metering roller of another size: a **larger** one if too little is applied, a **smaller** one if too much.
7. Calibrate the metering roller — see [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).

**Dispenser sensor with “Weight control” switched on — check, in this order:**

1. The target rate of the product.
2. The settings of the dispenser shaft sensor — see [Dispenser shaft sensor](dispenser-sensor.md).
3. The metering unit.
4. The dispenser sensor is serviceable.
5. Calibrate the dispenser — see [Calibrate the dispenser by weight](calibrate-dispenser-weight.md).

## “Product dosage is” / “impossible! Check product” / “rate and calibration!”

**What it means.** With the current settings and target rate, the product cannot be applied by weight at all: the lowest speed at which the metering rollers can deliver the rate is already at or above the highest. On the home screen a red product icon blinks in the right-hand column.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The target rates of the products — one product asking too much closes the window for all of them.
2. **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** of the speed sensor — see [Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).
3. The settings of the electric motors that apply the products by weight, above all **“Minimum, rpm”** and **“Maximum, rpm”**.
4. Calibrate the metering rollers of the electric motors.
5. If that does not help: fit metering rollers of another size.

> **TIP**
>
> The calibration screen of a metering motor shows the speed window the current roller allows. If it reads **“Can not provide dosage!”**, no calibration will help — the roller does not suit the rate. See [Calibrate a metering motor by weight](calibrate-motor-weight.md).


# User is Agronomist: alarms will not be shown

How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “User is Agronomist!” / “Alarms will not be shown!”

**What it means.** Seeding has started while the **“Agronomist”** or **“Service”** access level is set. At these levels the panel does not show alarm windows; this warning is the only exception. It appears **once** for the whole time you work at that level. Like every alarm of the panel itself, its text starts with the line **“HOME - close message”**; close it with **“Close”**.

![The warning window, with the Close button.](figures/five-alarm-agronomist)

**What to do:** set the access level back to **“Operator”**:

::: steps
1. Tap **“Close”** in the warning.

2. Tap the home screen with **two fingers**, then tap **“Settings”** twice.

3. Swipe up to **“User”** and tap it. Swipe left until it reads **“Operator”**.

4. Tap **“User”** again. Going down a level needs no PIN.
:::

Switching the panel off and on does the same: after every power-on the panel starts at **“Operator”**.

> **NOTE**
>
> **Expect a short run of alarms on the way back.** The alarms raised while the level was high have waited. The panel drops those that have gone away and shows the ones that are still true. It is the backlog, not a new fault. See [Access levels](access-levels.md).


# Travel speed sensor failed, speed limits contradict, or poor GPS signal

How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Speed sensor #1 failed” / “Speed sensor #2 failed”

**What it means.** The profile says the machine has **two** travel speed sensors, but the panel sees movement from only one of them. The number names the silent sensor. This alarm cannot appear on a machine with one speed sensor.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Check that both speed sensors are serviceable, and repair what you find.
2. If one sensor cannot be repaired now: change the system profile so that only one speed sensor is used — see [The profile](profile.md).

## “Error in settings of Min/Max”

**What it means.** The minimum and the maximum travel speed set for the speed sensor contradict each other. The panel cannot decide whether the current speed is allowed.

**What to do:** check **“Min speed, km/h”** and **“Max speed, km/h”** in the settings of the speed sensor. The minimum must be below the maximum. See [Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).

## “Poor GPS signal quality”

**What it means.** The speed is taken from the receiver built into the panel (**“GPS internal”** is **“Yes”**), and it sees **fewer than four satellites**. The speed it gives cannot be trusted. The satellite symbol on the home screen is red.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Give the panel a clear view of the sky; move off from under trees, buildings or a shed roof.
2. Watch the number beside the satellite symbol: it shows how many satellites the receiver uses. Wait until it reaches four or more.
3. If the reception stays poor, take the speed from the wheel sensor: set **“GPS internal”** to **“No”** — see [GPS](gps.md) and [Travel speed sensor](speed-sensor.md).

> **NOTE**
>
> **“SLOWER” and “FASTER” are not alarm windows.** When the speed leaves the permitted range, the speed field shows **“SLOWER”** or **“FASTER”** and, at the **“Operator”** level, the alarm sound plays until you correct the speed. See [Indicators](indicators.md#speed).


# Metering motor: jammed, electrical faults, bootloader

These alarms come from the controller that drives an electric motor of a dispenser. The name in the alarm window tells you which motor; the Motors screen shows which tile is in trouble ([Motors screen](motors-screen.md)). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “Motor jammed!”

**What it means.** The controller does not see rotation while the motor should be running.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The metering unit is serviceable and turns freely.
2. The rotation sensor of the motor is serviceable, and so is its connection to the controller — the cable and the connector.

If jams are frequent, **“Rollback when jammed”** lets the motor back off and try again — see [Dispenser electric motor](dispenser-motor.md).

## “Short circuit”

**What it means.** The controller has detected a short circuit.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The cable connection: the cables and the connector are intact.
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over current”

**What it means.** The current has gone above the limit. The window adds a line with the current the controller measured, in amperes.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The motor and the seeding mechanism for jamming.
2. The cable connection: the cables and the connector are intact.
3. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Under voltage”

**What it means.** The supply voltage of the motor is below the allowed value. The motor cannot run.

**Measure the supply voltage first.**

**If it is too low:**

1. The alternator is serviceable.
2. The tension of the alternator belts.
3. The power harness is connected firmly to the battery or the alternator terminals, as the required supply voltage demands.
4. The cable connections make reliable electrical contact.

**If the supply voltage is in order:** replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over voltage”

**What it means.** The supply voltage of the motor is above the allowed value. The motor cannot run.

**Measure the supply voltage first.**

**If it is too high:**

1. The alternator is serviceable.
2. The power harness is connected firmly to the battery or the alternator terminals, as the required supply voltage demands.
3. The cable connections make reliable electrical contact.

**If the supply voltage is in order:** replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “Over temperature”

**What it means.** The motor controller has overheated.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Let the motor cool down.
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.

## “FAILURE”

**What it means.** The controller has detected an unusual fault that needs the service support.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Read the fault code: touch and hold the motor tile → **“Information”** → line **“Last fault:”**. See [Read the fault code of an electric motor](motor-fault-codes.md).
2. Replace the controller with a serviceable one to test it.
3. Give the code and the number of the motor to the service support.

## “Device in bootloader!”

**What it means.** The controller has stayed in its firmware update mode and is not running its working program. It cannot drive the motor.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Switch the power off and on.
2. If the message returns, the firmware update of the controller was not completed. Call the service support.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> The liquid fertilizer pump controller raises the same electrical alarms — [Liquid fertilizer pump](alarms-pump-controller.md).


# Liquid fertilizer pump: pressure and rate alarms

The pump controller is built on the same electronics as the controller of a metering motor. Besides the alarms on this page it raises **the electrical alarms of the metering motor controller** — **“Short circuit”**, **“Over current”**, **“Under voltage”**, **“Over voltage”**, **“Over temperature”**, **“FAILURE”** and **“Device in bootloader!”** — with the same meaning and the same actions: see [Metering motor alarms](alarms-motor-controller.md). How the window works: [How alarms work](how-alarms-work.md).

## “High pressure”

**What it means.** The measured liquid pressure has reached **“Max pressure, Bar”**.

**What to do, in this order:**

1. Reduce the travel speed.
2. In the settings of the pump controller, check **“Max pressure, Bar”** and, if the line allows it, increase it — see [Liquid fertilizer](liquid-fertilizer.md).

## “Pressure sensor failure!”

**What it means.** The signal from the pressure sensor has fallen well below its 4–20 mA working range.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The connection of the sensor to the controller — the cable and the connector are intact.
2. **“Pressure sensor”** in the settings of the pump controller names the input the sensor is really wired to.
3. The sensor is serviceable. If it has failed, replace it.

The status screen of the pump controller shows the pressure and the raw sensor signal in mA — see [The sensor status screen](sensor-status-screen.md#what-each-kind-of-sensor-adds).

## “Rate low”

**What it means.** The pump controller cannot reach the set rate: the actual rate is below the target by more than **“Product rate error,%”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed and is reasonably steady.
2. The working load of the pump. **Above 90 %:** drive more slowly.
3. **Load under 90 %, or jumping strongly:** increase **“Product rate error,%”** in the **“Settings”** menu, at the **“Agronomist”** level — see [The Settings menu](settings-menu.md).
4. The pump is serviceable.

## “Rate high”

**What it means.** The pump controller applies more than the set rate: the actual rate is above the target by more than **“Product rate error,%”**.

**What to check, in this order:**

1. The travel speed on the panel matches the real speed and is reasonably steady.
2. The working load of the pump. **Under 10 %:** drive faster.
3. **Load above 10 %, or jumping strongly:** increase **“Product rate error,%”** in the **“Settings”** menu.
4. The pump is serviceable.


# Read the fault code of an electric motor

When a metering motor raises **“FAILURE”**, its controller also records a numeric code. Read it out and give it to the service support together with the number of the motor.

::: steps
1. Long swipe left on the home screen until the Motors screen appears ([Working screens](working-screens.md)). Touch and hold the tile of the faulty motor; its context menu opens. A motor tile on the second home screen works the same way.

2. Tap **“Information”**, and tap it again. The status screen of the motor opens.

3. Read the line **“Last fault:”**. The status of the motor reads **“Faulty”** while any of its alarms is active.
:::

The same code is shown as **“Error code”** on the Electric motors screen, at the **“Agronomist”** level — see [Motor controller diagnostics](motor-controller-diagnostics.md).

## The codes

The panel shows only the number. The descriptions come from the motor controller itself.

### Command and parameter errors

The controller refused something the panel asked of it.

| **Code** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| -250 | Invalid command |
| -251 | Unexpected command |
| -252 | Invalid command syntax |
| -253 | Invalid command arguments |
| -260 | Invalid number of arguments |
| -261 | Specified index is greater than FFFFh |
| -262 | Specified sub-index is greater than FFh |
| -300 | Parameter does not exist |
| -301 | Memory write operation failed |
| -302 | Restore operation failed |
| -306 | Parameter cannot be written |
| -307 | Parameter cannot be read |
| -308 | Parameter value out of range |
| -316 | Version of the stored parameter set does not match the firmware version |
| -318 | Stored parameter set has an invalid check sum |
| -322 | Parameter cannot be set: the axis is in motion |
| -325 | Parameter cannot be set: the positioning mode is inactive |
| -340 | Parameter cannot be set: a limit switch is active |
| -343 | Parameter cannot be set: a stop or halt command is being executed |
| -350 | Parameter not contained in the specified index |
| -351 | Parameter not contained in the specified sub-index |

### Device errors

The controller or the motor itself is in trouble.

| **Code** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| -1000 | Low supply voltage |
| -1001 | Excessive supply voltage |
| -1002 | Low electronics supply voltage |
| -1003 | Excessive electronics supply voltage |
| -1020 | Overtemperature of the device |
| -1021 | Overtemperature of the heat sink |
| -1060 | Short circuit of a motor lead: between motor leads, motor and ground, or motor and power supply |
| -1061 | Motor overcurrent |
| -4000 | Following-difference error in the motion sequence |
| -5100 | Limit switch active |


# Touch zones and gestures on every screen

The Hectare 5 has no buttons; every action is a gesture on the screen. Each screen listens only to its own gestures and ignores the rest. With **“Buttons sound”** set to **“Yes”**, every gesture the screen takes is confirmed with a click.

## Kinds of touch

|  | **Gesture** | **How** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-tap.svg){height=46px} | Tap | One finger, touch and lift within half a second. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-hold.svg){height=46px} | Touch and hold | One finger kept on one spot for more than half a second. The panel reacts while the finger is still down. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-double-tap.svg){height=46px} | Double tap | Two quick taps with one finger. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-two-finger-tap.svg){height=46px} | Two-finger tap | One tap with two fingers at once. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-three-finger-tap.svg){height=46px} | Three-finger tap | One tap with three fingers at once. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-swipe.svg){height=46px} | Swipe | A short stroke of one finger across the screen. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-long-swipe.svg){height=46px} | Long swipe | A stroke of one finger across more than a third of the screen. |
| ![](figures/icons/gesture-two-finger-swipe.svg){height=46px} ![](figures/icons/gesture-long-two-finger-swipe.svg){height=46px} | Two-finger swipe, long two-finger swipe | The same with two fingers. |

## Home screen

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Two-finger tap | Opens the main menu. |
| Touch and hold a device — icon or column | Opens its context menu. |
| Touch and hold a diagram, then swipe up or down | Lights the diagram's target and changes it, one step per swipe. |
| Tap outside the diagrams | Ends the change of a target. |
| Touch and hold a kg/ha indicator | Opens the number pad for that product's target rate. |
| Touch and hold an empty place of the right-hand column | Locks or unlocks product application. One short beep confirms. Machines with dispenser motors or a pump only. |
| Double tap | Sets the alarm level from the rate being applied. Only while applying. |
| Long swipe left | Table (Statistics, if there is no Table). |
| Long swipe right | Second home screen. |

## Second home screen

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Tap the settings symbol | Opens the main menu. |
| Tap the GPS symbol | Opens the GPS screen; a long swipe up leaves it. |
| Tap a red or green chevron | Takes a motor out of or into control. |
| Tap the unit value | Shows the next unit — fan, pressure, pump. |
| Touch and hold the rate, then swipe up or down | Changes the seeding rate. |
| Touch and hold the stop symbol | Locks or unlocks product application. |
| Touch and hold a motor, the speed or a unit value | Opens its context menu. |
| Long swipe left | Back to the home screen. |

## Table

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Long two-finger swipe right or left | Next or previous table. |
| Swipe up or down | Scroll the lines. |
| Two-finger tap | Asks **“Zero readings?”**. |
| Long swipe left | Statistics. There is no gesture back. |

## Statistics

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Swipe up or down | Scroll the report, one line per swipe. |
| Two-finger swipe right or left | Show the next or the previous field. |
| Two-finger tap | Menu of the screen. |
| Long swipe left | Motors, or the home screen if there is none. There is no gesture back. |

## Motors

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Long swipe left | Home screen. |
| Long swipe right | Statistics. |
| Touch and hold a tile | Context menu of that motor or actuator. |

## Status screen of a device

Opened with **“Information”** in a context menu.

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Swipe right or left | The next or the previous device. |
| Swipe up, or three-finger tap | Back. |

## Tramline rhythm form

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Swipe up or down | Move between lines. |
| Swipe right or left | Move along a line; on **“Rhythm”**, step through the rhythms. |
| Two-finger tap | Opens the selected cell. |
| Touch and hold | Saves the rhythm without leaving. |
| Three-finger tap | Saves the rhythm and returns to the Tramline menu. |

## In a menu

| **Gesture** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Tap an item | Selects it. |
| Tap the selected item again | Enters it: opens its menu, runs its action, or opens the number pad. |
| Touch and hold an item | Selects and enters it at once. |
| Swipe right or left | Raises or lowers the value of the **selected** item by one step. For a value in square brackets, opens the number pad. |
| Swipe up or down | Scrolls the list. |
| Tap outside the menu, or three-finger tap | Leaves the menu. |

## Number pad

| **Touch** | **What it does** |
| --- | --- |
| Tap the digits | Type the value. |
| Tap **“OK”** | Accept the value. |
| Tap outside the pad | Leave without changing anything. |
| Touch and hold the backspace | Clear the value. |

## Windows

| **Window** | **Touch** |
| --- | --- |
| **Question** — blue strip, buttons | Tap **“Yes”** — confirm. Tap **“No”** — refuse. Tap outside the window — cancel. |
| **Information** — blue or red strip, no buttons | Closes by itself after about two seconds, or with a tap inside the window. |
| **Alarm** — red bar **“FAILURE!”** | Tap **“Close”** — close this alarm. No other touch works. |


# Terms

## Gestures

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Tap** | One finger, touch and lift at once. |
| **Touch and hold** | One finger kept on one spot for more than half a second. |
| **Long swipe** | A stroke of one finger across more than a third of the screen. It moves between the working screens. |
| **Two-finger tap** | One tap with two fingers at once. On the home screen it opens the main menu. |

All gestures: [Touch zones and gestures](buttons-and-gestures.md).

## Rates and control

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Rate** | The target intensity the operator sets. The panel compares the actual intensity against it and reports a deviation that is too large. |
| **Rate error** | How far the actual intensity may stand from the rate before that becomes an alarm. Set per sensor group, in per cent (**“Rate error,%”**). For products by weight and the pump the setting is **“Product rate error,%”**. |
| **Product application control** | The panel does not judge the sowing at every moment: it starts watching once the conditions are met — the implement is lowered and moving. Until then a silent section is not a fault. |
| **Alarm level** | In the “Flow” mode, the lowest intensity still counted as normal — the control line of the diagram. Below it the section is reported, whatever the neighbours do. See [The section diagram](section-diagram.md). |
| **Path interval** | The stretch of the run over which skips, doubles and the other figures are gathered before they are redrawn. Set by **“Recalculation,m”**, which the panel renames **“Recalculation,sec”** when the seeding mode counts in seconds instead of metres. |
| **Share of sowing rows** | The share of rows that must sow for the panel to decide that the machine is seeding — **“Percent of sowing,%”**, 20 % by default. |
| **Manual lock** | Stopping all product application by hand, with a touch and hold on an empty place of the right-hand column of the home screen. A yellow hand shows the lock is on. See [Lock product application by hand](lock-application-by-hand.md). |
| **Control (of a sensor)** | Whether the panel watches a sensor. A sensor out of control is shown with **!** and reports nothing. See [Take a sensor into or out of control](sensor-in-and-out-of-control.md). |
| **Imitation** | A simulated travel speed, set in the speed sensor, used when the speed sensor has failed. See [Work without the speed sensor](work-without-speed-sensor.md). |

## Seeding control modes

| **Mode** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Precise”** | Seeds per metre, with skips and doubles — row-crop planters. |
| **“Flow”** | Seeds per second against an alarm level — grain drills. |
| **“Hybrid”** | Seeds per metre, with a rate error as in “Precise”; the alarm level can be set automatically as in “Flow”. |

## Sensors

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Section control sensor** | The common name for a seed, dry fertilizer or liquid fertilizer sensor. One per section of the implement. |
| **Seed sensor** | Counts the seed passing one section. On a **row-crop planter** it also separates **doubles** and **skips**; on a grain drill it measures intensity only — the seeds arrive too close together to be told apart. |
| **Dry fertilizer sensor** | The same device, watching a granular fertilizer line. |
| **Liquid fertilizer sensor** | A flow meter counting the volume through one section. |
| **Speed sensor** | Measures the travel speed. Distance, area and every rate are calculated from it. On the Hectare 5 the speed can also come from the built-in GPS receiver. |
| **Dispenser sensor** | Watches that the dispenser shaft turns. |
| **Fan sensor** | Watches the fan speed against a set minimum and maximum. |
| **Pressure sensor** | Watches positive pressure or vacuum, depending on how it is plumbed. |
| **Hopper sensor** | Reports when the product has fallen below the point where the sensor sits. |
| **Work position sensor** | Tells the panel whether the implement is lowered into work or raised for transport. |
| **Marker sensors** | Report which mechanical marker is down, so that the tramline bout can advance by itself. |

## Tramline

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **Tramline** | A driving lane left unsown, made by shutting off one or several sections on chosen bouts. |
| **Rhythm** | The repeating sequence of bouts, with the bouts marked on which particular sections must not sow. See [Set up the tramline rhythm](tramline-rhythm.md). |
| **Bout** | One pass of the implement across the field. The rhythm counts them and returns to the first when it runs out. |
| **Tramline actuator** | The device that shuts the sections off. A machine can have up to four. |

## Devices

| **Term** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- |
| **HUB8** (input device; in the menus **“Concentrator-8”**) | An eight-channel hub for sensors that have no controller of their own. It watches them and reports each to the panel as if it were a device. |
| **Electric motor controller** | Drives one or two dispenser motors, or the liquid fertilizer pump. |
| **microSD** | The memory card, for reports. |
| **Profile** | The list of what the machine carries. The panel draws its screens from it. See [Profile](profile.md). |

## Access levels

| **Level** | **What it is for** |
| --- | --- |
| **“Operator”** | The level the panel starts at after every power-on. Everyday work. Only at this level are alarm windows shown. |
| **“Agronomist”** | The commissioning settings, the machine profile and the address set-up of the devices. Needs a **PIN**. |
| **“Service”** | The reset items and the service settings. Used by the service department; needs its own PIN. |

The level is chosen in **“Settings”** → **“User”**. Details: [Access levels](access-levels.md).
